title: Cabo Verde Olympians strengthen communities through sport and solidarity
body:
The National Olympians Association (NOA) of Cabo Verde is making a positive impact through a series of community initiatives, bringing people together, supporting young people and promoting the Olympic values of friendship, respect and excellence.

Under the leadership of NOA President Ismenia Fredérico OLY, the Association continues to demonstrate how Olympians can make a meaningful difference beyond the field of play, using sport as a platform for social inclusion, education and solidarity.

Supporting young people through education

In September, to mark the beginning of the new school year, the Cabo Verde NOA organised a solidarity campaign to collect school supplies and sports shoes for children and young people from disadvantaged backgrounds.

With the support of the local community and municipal authorities, the initiative helped ensure that students could return to school with the materials and appropriate footwear they needed, giving them a positive start to the academic year.

The campaign highlighted the importance of community solidarity and the role Olympians can play in creating opportunities for the next generation.

Raising awareness through Pink October

The Association has also supported Pink October, the international breast cancer awareness campaign, through a community initiative involving teachers and parents of secondary school students.

By bringing together members of the school community, the activity aimed to raise awareness of breast cancer and encourage collective engagement with an important public health issue.

Bringing generations together through sport

As part of the celebrations marking Cabo Verde's National Sports Day in November, the NOA is joining forces with the Institute of Sport and Youth to organise a large community walk, followed by a mass aerobics session.

The initiative, particularly aimed at young people and older adults, forms part of the Projeto Movidoso, which promotes active ageing and strengthens connections between generations through physical activity.

By encouraging people of different ages to participate together, the event will celebrate the power of sport to promote health, wellbeing and social inclusion.

Celebrating solidarity and Olympic values

Looking ahead to the festive season, the Cabo Verde NOA is also preparing a special Christmas solidarity event in the interior of Santiago Island.

The planned celebration will bring together community members of all ages through traditional games, inspiring talks with Olympians, theatre performances and poetry recitals.

Designed to encourage sharing, cultural exchange and intergenerational connections, the event aims to create a memorable day of solidarity and togetherness.

Olympians making a difference

Through these initiatives, the Cabo Verde NOA continues to demonstrate the important role National Olympians Associations play in their communities.

From supporting education and raising health awareness to encouraging active lifestyles and bringing generations together, the Association is helping ensure that the Olympic values continue to inspire positive change long beyond the Games.

Once an Olympian, always an Olympian.

title: Monaco Olympians celebrate 30th anniversary
body:
The NOA of Monaco has celebrated its 30th anniversary, bringing together Olympians and members of the Olympic Family in Monaco to mark the special occasion. Founded in the same year as WOA, the Monégasque NOA shares this 30-year milestone with the global organisation representing Olympians worldwide.

WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY joined Monaco NOA President Jérémy Bottin OLY and members of the Monégasque Olympian community for the anniversary celebrations, alongside WOA Patron HSH Prince Albert II of Monaco OLY, who has a longstanding connection with both organisations and competed for Monaco in bobsleigh at five Olympic Winter Games.

The event celebrated the Association’s history and the generations of Olympians who have represented Monaco on the world’s biggest sporting stage, as well as its continued commitment to promoting the Olympic values within the community.

WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY congratulated the Association on reaching the milestone.

 “It was a great pleasure to join our fellow Olympians in Monaco for this very special celebration. National Olympians Associations play an incredibly important role in keeping Olympians connected and ensuring that their experience and the Olympic values continue to have an impact long after their competitive careers have ended. Congratulations to Jérémy and the entire Monégasque Olympian community on this wonderful milestone.”

Monaco NOA President Jérémy Bottin OLY said the 30th anniversary was an opportunity to celebrate the Association’s history while looking ahead to its future.

“We are very proud to celebrate this important milestone together with our Olympians and friends from across the Olympic Movement. Our Association is built around the special bond that exists between Olympians, and we look forward to continuing to bring our community together and pass on the Olympic values to future generations.”

WOA congratulates the Monégasque NOA and its members on this special anniversary and looks forward to continuing to work together to support and connect Olympians in Monaco and beyond.

title: Olympian for Life Simidele Adeagbo OLY opens latest grants for female athletes after reaching $100,000 milestone
body:
WOA Olympians for Life awardee Simidele Adeagbo OLY is continuing to turn her own Olympic journey into opportunities for the next generation, as the SimiSleighs Foundation opens applications for its 2027 Athlete Grant Program.

The new application cycle comes as the Foundation celebrates an important milestone, having now awarded $100,000 USD in direct grant funding to elite female athletes pursuing their Olympic and Paralympic dreams.

Founded by Adeagbo, the SimiSleighs Foundation is a powerful example of the impact Olympians can continue to make after their own Olympic journeys. Through the Foundation, she is using her experience, platform and network as an Olympian to help other women overcome barriers, develop as leaders and fulfil their potential both on and off the field of play.

It is this commitment to creating positive change through sport that saw Adeagbo recognised by WOA as an Olympians for Life awardee.

The Foundation's Athlete Grant Program, launched in 2023, combines direct financial assistance with a six-month virtual development programme. Selected athletes can receive grants of up to $5,000 USD towards their training and competition expenses, while also benefiting from leadership and professional development, mentoring and connections with a global network of athletes and experts.

Having already reached $100,000 in direct athlete funding, SimiSleighs has set its sights even higher. The Foundation aims to award $1 million USD in grants to elite female athletes over the next decade, further extending the impact of Adeagbo's commitment to giving back through sport.

Applications are now open for the 2027 programme to female athletes training towards the Los Angeles 2028 or Alpes 2030 Olympic or Paralympic Games. The programme will run from January to June 2027. Full eligibility requirements and programme criteria are available on the SimiSleighs Foundation website.

The deadline to apply is Friday, 16 October 2026 at 11:59pm EST.

Find out more about the programme, eligibility criteria and how to apply:
https://www.simisleighsfoundation.org/athlete-grant-program

title: Jamaican Olympians and global Olympians community rebuild STETHS after Hurricane Melissa
body:
Months after Jamaican Olympians appealed to the worldwide Olympian community for help, the response has rebuilt a home for the next generation of student-athletes at St. Elizabeth Technical High School (STETHS).

When Hurricane Melissa tore through Jamaica, it left the girls' dormitory at STETHS — one of the island's most storied sporting institutions — in urgent need of repair. The Olympians Association of Jamaica launched a GoFundMe appeal to restore the dormitory roof and protect a safe, stable home for the young female student-athletes who depend on it.

That appeal was answered. Together, Olympians and supporters worldwide raised J$2 million for the rebuild. The campaign has since closed, the funds have been delivered to the Olympians Association of Jamaica, and the girls' dormitory is once again up and running — its residents back learning, training and dreaming under a secure roof.

Chris Stokes, a member of the Olympians Association of Jamaica who was part of the initiative, said: "STETHS has shaped Jamaican athletes for generations. Seeing the global Olympian family step up to protect that legacy — and get these young women back into a safe dormitory — has been genuinely moving."

For the Jamaican Olympians, the rebuild is about more than a roof. STETHS has shaped generations of Jamaican Olympians, and restoring it means the next generation can keep growing in a place that has always dreamed bigger. NAJO thanks every member of the global Olympian family who gave proof of what the community can do when it comes together for its own.

title: Olympian community called on to support Nepal following devastating floods
body:
The World Olympians Association is joining WOA Executive Committee member Deepak Bista OLY in calling on the global Olympian community to support the people of Nepal following the devastating floods that have struck the country.

On 26 August, a catastrophic flood swept through areas of northern Nepal, causing widespread loss of life and extensive damage to homes, roads and critical infrastructure. Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha are among the districts severely affected, with search, rescue and relief operations continuing across the region.

Deepak Bista OLY, who represented Nepal in taekwondo at the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games and carried his country's flag at the Opening Ceremony, has appealed to his fellow Olympians to stand with those affected.

“Nepal is facing a devastating flood and landslide crisis,” said Bista. “I humbly appeal to WOA and our entire Olympic family for any support possible for the affected people. Every help matters. Together, we can make a difference.”

Bista and his family are safe, but communities across the affected regions have suffered devastating losses.

The Government of Nepal has launched an official appeal for financial assistance to support ongoing search, rescue, relief and rehabilitation efforts. Donations can be made directly to the Government of Nepal's Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund, including by international credit or debit card.

WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY said: “Our thoughts are with Deepak, Nepal's Olympians and everyone affected by this terrible disaster. The strength of our Olympian community lies in standing together, particularly at times of great need. We encourage Olympians around the world who are able to help to support the official relief efforts.”

WOA extends its deepest sympathies to everyone who has lost family members, friends and loved ones, and stands in solidarity with the people of Nepal as rescue and recovery efforts continue.

You can support the official Government of Nepal relief effort here: 
https://pmdrf.nchl.com.np/

title: WOA Mourns the Passing of Three-Time Olympian, King Harald V of Norway
body:
The World Olympians Association is saddened to learn of the passing of His Majesty King Harald V of Norway, a three-time Olympian and lifelong member of the Olympic and sporting community, who died on 28 August 2026 at the age of 89.

Long before ascending to the Norwegian throne in 1991, King Harald represented his country as an athlete on the Olympic stage. A passionate and accomplished sailor, he competed at three consecutive Olympic Games; Tokyo 1964, Mexico City 1968 and Munich 1972.

At his first Olympic Games in Tokyo in 1964, the then Crown Prince Harald was given the honour of carrying the Norwegian flag at the Opening Ceremony. Competing in the three-person keelboat event, he and his crew finished eighth. He returned to compete at Mexico City 1968 and Munich 1972, completing an Olympic career spanning three editions of the Games.

His passion for sailing continued throughout his life. In 1987, King Harald and his crew became world champions in offshore sailing aboard Fram X, and he later added a European title in 2005. Remarkably, he continued competing in national and international regattas well into his eighties, bringing his competitive sailing career to a close only in 2022.

King Harald also maintained a close connection with the wider Olympic Movement throughout his life. He officially opened the Lillehammer 1994 Olympic Winter Games and was awarded the Olympic Order in Gold that same year in recognition of his contribution to the Olympic Movement.

His lifelong commitment to sport extended far beyond his own achievements as an athlete. He remained a passionate supporter of Norwegian athletes and was a familiar presence at Olympic Games and sporting events around the world, most recently supporting Norway's athletes at the Milano Cortina 2026 Olympic Winter Games.

King Harald's life represented an extraordinary connection between Olympism, public service and a genuine lifelong love of sport. From carrying his country's flag into the Olympic Stadium in Tokyo as a young Olympian to supporting new generations of athletes more than six decades later, sport remained a constant throughout his life.

The World Olympians Association extends its deepest condolences to the Royal Family, the Norwegian Olympic community, Norway's Olympians and the people of Norway.

title: WOA and IOC Meet to Discuss Transition and Next Steps
body:
The World Olympians Association (WOA) Executive Committee met with representatives of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) on 17 August 2026 to discuss the next steps following the IOC Executive Board's decision to terminate the Cooperation and Licence Agreement (CLA).

The meeting provided an important opportunity for members of the WOA Executive Committee to seek further clarification regarding the decision and to engage constructively with the IOC on the practical arrangements and priorities for the transition period ahead.

The IOC confirmed its intention to continue supporting the core administrative needs of WOA throughout the remaining period of the CLA, including costs associated with facilitating an orderly transition process.

The IOC also provided further information regarding the planned consultation process on the future engagement and representation of Olympians. The consultation will be led by the IOC Athletes' Commission, with the support of an independent professional agency, and is expected to commence in the coming months.

During the meeting, WOA Executive Committee members emphasised the significant experience, contribution and global reach of National Olympians Associations (NOAs) around the world. They highlighted the important role NOAs have played in connecting, supporting and engaging Olympians within their respective countries and communities.

WOA remains committed to representing the interests of its members and the wider Olympian community throughout this period of transition and to engaging constructively in the process ahead.

WOA will continue to keep its members and the wider Olympian community informed as the transition progresses and as further information regarding the IOC-led consultation becomes available.

title: 2026 applications open for full scholarships with the University of London
body:
This programme is delivered entirely in English, which is why this story is only available in English.

Applications for the scholarship PGCert Scholarship Programme are now open. To apply, fill in the application form here.

Applications are now open for the 2026 World Olympians Association (WOA) Scholarship Programme, providing Olympians with the opportunity to undertake the Postgraduate Certificate in International Sports Management online through the prestigious University of London.

WOA is offering two full scholarships to Olympians from around the world, together with two 50% scholarships & thirty 25% Scholarships, enabling more members of the Olympian community to gain a globally recognised postgraduate qualification while balancing their sporting, professional and personal commitments.

Delivered fully online, the programme is flexible and designed to fit around the busy schedules of elite athletes. Participants can study from anywhere in the world and progress at a pace that suits their individual circumstances.

Developed in partnership with the World Academy of Sport (WAoS) and the University of London, the programme equips Olympians with the knowledge and practical skills required to pursue leadership and management careers across the global sport industry. Subjects include sport governance, leadership, marketing, finance, strategy, integrity, and the business of international sport.

Since the scholarship programme was established in 2020, more than 70 Olympians have successfully completed the qualification, with many progressing into leadership roles within sport organisations, National Olympic Committees, International Federations, and the wider sport industry.

The next intake for the programme commences in September 2026.

For more information about the Postgraduate Certificate in International Sports Management, including entry requirements and programme details, click here.

Scholarship applications close on 19 August 2026.

title: New research-backed programme helps Olympians navigate identity, wellbeing and social connection after retirement from sport
body:
For many Olympians, stepping away from elite sport marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter. Yet, it can also bring unexpected challenges. Questions around identity, purpose and belonging are common as athletes transition into life beyond competition.

Research conducted by KU Leuven (Belgium) and international university partners shows that this transition can have a significant impact on athletes' wellbeing. Studies have found that many former elite athletes experience psychological challenges after retirement from sport, with feelings of loss of identity and purpose being among the most frequently reported experiences.

To help address these challenges, researchers have developed More Than Sport – a free, research-based programme designed specifically for retired elite athletes. The programme helps participants better understand the identity transition that accompanies retirement from elite sport and provides practical tools to strengthen social connections, resilience and wellbeing.

Early participants have described the programme as an important opportunity to feel understood and realise that many of the emotions experienced during retirement from sport are shared by fellow athletes. Several highlighted that it was the first time their identity transition—not simply their next career step—had been placed at the centre of the conversation.

Take Part in the Study

The research team is currently conducting a large-scale intervention study and is inviting Olympians to participate free of charge.

You may be eligible if you:

  • Stopped competing at the highest level within the past two years; or
  • Recently transitioned from elite competition to a lower competitive or recreational level;
  • Speak English or Dutch.

Participants will receive:

  • Free access to the More Than Sport programme;
  • Personal guidance from a researcher;
  • Five online modules and short video calls throughout the programme.

Even if you are not eligible yourself, you may know an Olympian or recently retired athlete who could benefit from taking part.

To learn more about the programme and the science behind it, please read the attached fact sheet and visit: 
https://www.leadinginsights.be/en/research/identitytransitions

To learn more about participating in the study, visit: 
https://www.leadinginsights.be/en/research/identitytransitions/rct

title: Ensuring Continuity for the Global Olympian Community
body:
The WOA took note of the IOC's notification of termination of the Agreement signed between the WOA and the IOC in September 2025. The WOA accepts that the IOC uses a right both parties of the Agreement have. There is no need to give any reason for termination.

The WOA expressed its willingness to support the IOC in the engagement process with the Olympian community so that a best possible respect of the initiatives the WOA and its constituencies, the NOAs, could realise and uphold in thirty years since their foundation, will be given. The WOA proposed to the IOC to jointly set up an Olympian Community Liaison Group for elaborating all necessary details for a splendid future for the Olympians and their NOAs.

title: GB Olympians mark 50 years since the Montreal and Innsbruck Games
body:
To mark the 50th anniversary of the Montreal Summer Games and the Innsbruck Winter Games, Great Britain's 1976 Olympians came together in London for a special reunion hosted by the GB Olympians Association. Over 80 Olympians attended the event, which took place at the Lansdowne Club in Mayfair, a private members' club in central London which counts several Olympians among its members.

Among the guests was HRH The Princess Royal, who competed for Great Britain in equestrian events at the Montreal Games. Also among the guests was Dame Katherine Grainger OLY, Chair of the British Olympic Association.

Sarah Lewis OLY, Chair of the GB Olympians Association, said: 'It was a truly memorable evening. Seeing athletes from various sports come together to share memories, renew friendships, and celebrate their lifelong connection to the Olympic Movement was a privilege. The strength of that bond remains as powerful today as it was in 1976 — Once an Olympian, Always an Olympian.'

Following the event, the Private Secretary of HRH The Princess Royal shared: 'Her Royal Highness was delighted to attend and very much enjoyed the opportunity to spend time with fellow Olympians and reflect on the 1976 Games. She was touched by the warmth of the welcome and the chance to speak with so many guests.'

A particular highlight of the evening was the commemorative film, which featured archive footage from the International Olympic Committee and BBC Sport and had been edited by postgraduate students.

Several Olympians who had lost touch reconnected on the night and are now planning their own gatherings. It is a reminder that the Olympic Games create bonds that last a lifetime.

title: Olympians at the heart of the Olympic Games, a milestone decision was taken today
body:
Dear fellow Olympians,

Today at the 146th IOC session in Lausanne, a milestone decision was taken. The chair of the IOC athletes commission, Mr Pau Gasol OLY, announced that all athletes who competed in the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympic Games will be eligible to apply for a 10 000 USD grant.

Please see the story for reference: https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/an-olympic-first-ioc-to-set-up-fit-for-the-future-olympian-grant-to-support-all-olympians-with-usd-10-000-starting-from-milano-cortina-2026.

I am truly encouraged by this decision from the IOC and its commitment to both current and future generations of Olympians. I would like to commend the Chair of the IOC Athletes’ Commission, Mr Pau Gasol OLY, and the IOC President, Mrs Kirsty Coventry OLY, for their continued investment in Olympians and the wider Olympic community.  I also applaud the IOC’s belief in building a “Strong Olympian Community,” recognising that Olympians remain an important part of the Olympic Movement long after their competitive careers have ended. The WOA is proud to support this vision and help deliver these important messages through our network of 115 National Olympians Associations worldwide.

Best Olympian regards,

Pernilla Wiberg OLY
President

title: Slovenian Olympians Strengthen Their Connection to the Global Olympian Community
body:
Olympians from across Slovenia came together at a special gathering of the Slovenian NOA, held alongside a charity volleyball event supporting young athletes and para-athletes from disadvantaged backgrounds.

The event provided an opportunity to celebrate Slovenia's Olympians and recognise their place within the global Olympian community through an OLY ceremony. By awarding OLY certificates and pins, the Slovenian NOA is helping Olympians maintain a lifelong connection to the Olympic Movement and a worldwide network of fellow Olympians.

Among those receiving OLY certificates were Olympic champions, medallists and Olympians representing a wide range of sports, including alpine skiing, athletics, swimming, judo, handball, canoeing, ski jumping, tennis, archery and volleyball.

Olympians were welcomed by Franjo Bobinac, President of the Olympic Committee of Slovenia, and Iztok Cop OLY, President of the Slovenian NOA, who highlighted the importance of maintaining strong connections within the Olympic community and promoting the values of Olympism beyond competition.

The gathering also featured a conversation with Olympian and Slovenian volleyball player Dejan Vincic OLY, who reflected on his Olympic journey and the significance of representing his country at the Olympic Games.

The Olympians' gathering took place during a charity volleyball day led by Olympian and Slovenian national volleyball team captain Tine Urnaut OLY, ambassador of the 'Botrstvo v športu' programme ('Godparenthood in Sport'). Through ticket sales, donations and fundraising activities, the initiative has already raised more than €100,000 this year to support young athletes and para-athletes from disadvantaged backgrounds. The event also attracted widespread public attention, with the celebrity teams coached by the President of Slovenia, Nataša Pirc Musar, and well-known comedian Lado Bizovicar.

Set against the backdrop of a community-focused sporting event, the gathering showcased the power of Olympians coming together across generations and sporting disciplines. Through initiatives such as OLY ceremonies and regular Olympian gatherings, the Slovenian NOA helps ensure that Olympians remain connected, engaged and recognised as valued members of the global Olympian community long after their sporting careers have ended.

title: “School to Olympic” Program Inspires Students in Nepalgunj
body:
The Nepal Olympic Association (NOA) continued its commitment to inspiring the next generation through sport by successfully delivering the “School to Olympic” program in Nepalgunj, Lumbini Province, on May 8, 2026. Organised by the Nepal Olympians Association, the initiative marked the program's 17th location and engaged more than 200 students in an unforgettable interaction with Nepal’s Olympians.

As part of the NOA’s annual schedule, the “School to Olympic” program is planned to reach 6–8 locations across the country each year, bringing the Olympic spirit directly into schools and communities. The Nepalgunj edition once again highlighted the power of Olympians to inspire young people through education, personal stories, and shared experiences.

Hosted at APF School Kohalpur, the 2026 edition of the program introduced students to Olympism, the Olympic Movement, and the core Olympic values of excellence, friendship, and respect. Through open discussions and interactive sessions, Olympians shared their personal journeys, challenges, and achievements, encouraging students to dream big and pursue sports with dedication and discipline.

The event also included practical self-defense demonstrations and motivational activities designed to connect sport with confidence, leadership, and service to society. Students enthusiastically engaged with the athletes, asking questions and learning firsthand about the commitment required to compete at the highest level.

Mayor Purna Prasad Acharya praised the initiative and underlined the importance of combining education and sport to empower the younger generation. He expressed the municipality’s commitment to supporting the expansion of the program to schools across the region from next year, ensuring that even more students have the opportunity to meet Olympians and hear their inspiring stories.

The Nepal Olympians Association believes that programs such as “School to Olympic” play an important role in shaping future generations by promoting healthy lifestyles, resilience, teamwork, and the values of the Olympic Movement. Through direct engagement with Olympians, students are encouraged not only to pursue sporting excellence but also to become positive contributors to their communities.

By bringing Olympians and students together, the “School to Olympic” program continues to demonstrate how the Olympic spirit can inspire, educate, and create lasting impact far beyond the field of play.

title: Olympians send messages of support to Children’s Hospital in Milan
body:
The OLY House Hub in Milan during the Olympic Games perfectly expressed the WOA’s mission of Service to Olympians, Service to Society. The Hub was a great service for Olympians, but it also gave them the opportunity to give something special to the children of Milan who were hospital bound.

Metro 5 kindly gave the WOA a space at their Monumentale station for the duration of the Games. What began as a location became something far greater, an OLY House Hub where Olympians from across the world gathered, reconnected, enjoyed each other’s company and added their signatures and messages of hope and support to a growing wall of Olympic voices. Every word on that wall was dedicated to one place: the Buzzi Children's Hospital in Milan, which is supported by Metro 5.

Metro 5 Technical Director Diego Polotti said: "The poster signed by Olympians who visited the OLY House Hub at the Monumentale M5 station during the Olympic Games is a gift for the hospital's children and today finds its home at the Buzzi Hospital. There are many positive messages about sport, energy, and sharing for the youngest patients. With this gesture, Metro 5, together with Fondazione Buzzi, strengthens its commitment to bringing value to the city."

WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY made the journey back to Milan to personally hand over the poster to the hospital and said: "It was an honour to deliver the poster directly to the hospital. After talking with doctors, nurses, administrators, and the hospital clowns, I went to say hello to the children. It was so inspiring. I could see the spark in their eyes when I was telling them about my Olympic journey, what I learned, the lessons for them and what hosting the Olympic Games meant to their city and their country in the eyes of the world.”

Pernilla concluded: “I’d just like to remind all Olympians that you have the power to make a real difference. Sharing your journey and inspiring others, that is Olympism at its best. That is what we do. That’s in our DNA. Please go out there and tell your stories, the world needs it."

title: European NOAs in action
body:
Greek Olympians gather for a memorable annual meeting filled with pride and shared values

In March 2026, Greek Olympians came together for their annual meeting — an evening of warmth, pride, and genuine Olympic spirit that reunited athletes who have represented Greece on sport's greatest stage.

A highlight of the evening was the presentation of OLY pins to Olympians who had not yet received them. Among those honoured was Yann Genty, OLY, French Olympic gold medalist in handball at Paris 2024, who currently competes with AEK Athens and was warmly welcomed by the Greek Olympians in a gesture of friendship and shared Olympic values.

The evening also brought an important announcement: Voula Kozompoli, OLY, President of the Greek Olympians, has been elected to the Executive Board of the World Olympians Association, a proud recognition for her and for the entire Greek Olympians community.

The gathering was further distinguished by the presence of Spyros Capralos, OLY, President of the European Olympic Committees and IOC member for Greece, and Giorgos Mavrotas, OLY, General Secretary of the Ministry of Sports. More than an annual meeting, this was a celebration of shared memories, lasting friendships, and the enduring values that unite Olympians across generations and borders.

Cyprus Olympians launch animated Fair Play campaign in cinemas across the island

The Cyprus Olympians Association has unveiled an animated video celebrating Fair Play, a value at the heart of the Olympic spirit, as part of its ongoing commitment to promoting Olympism among younger generations and the wider public.

The video was created through the initiative and financial support of Dr. Andros Karapatakis, OLY, Vice President of the Cyprus Olympians Association and Cyprus' appointed Fair Play Ambassador for 2025–2026. Through vibrant animation, it conveys the importance of respect, integrity, and sportsmanship in a way that is accessible to audiences of all ages.

The video is being screened throughout April and May 2026 in theatres across Cyprus. The Cyprus Olympians Association warmly invites the World Olympians Association community to watch and share it within their own networks, helping carry the message of Fair Play to the global Olympian family.

Watch the video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hTsKDGHoDPs

title: OLYPAN: Panamanian Olympians Inspiring New Generations
body:
OLYPAN (Atletas Olimpicos de Panamá) has been running a notable Service to Society initiative involving workshops that bring Olympic athletes together with children and teenagers in schools. March 26 marked the fourth workshop organized by OLYPAN. These workshops introduce the Olympic spirit to new generations in a personal and hands-on manner.

This initiative was developed by the OLYPAN EXCO, chaired by Barbra Higgins Arana OLY, and formalized at their first annual meeting in June 2024. During this meeting, the Olympians recognised the importance of giving back to society, particularly to young people, by launching a truly inspiring and impactful initiative.

"Connecting Olympians with young people positively influences them, not only through sport, but also through the Olympic values that stay with us throughout our lives."

Each workshop is organised in coordination with a host school and involves a group of Olympians from different disciplines. For approximately two hours, students participate in presentations, discussions, video screenings, and sports activities, facilitating direct and enriching interaction with the Olympians.

The impact of these meetings has been significant. Young people are enthusiastic about hearing real-life stories of hard work and overcoming adversity, while teachers value educational contribution.

title: Apply now for WOA Grants
body:
The WOA 2026 Grants programme is now open. Olympians can apply for funding for projects run through your NOA which either benefit your fellow Olympians or promote physical activity in your community. More information on how to apply HERE.

NOAs can also apply for the annual Development Grant. See the end of this story for more details.

Here are a few examples of WOA funded projects delivered by NOAs and Olympians in the past.

The Zambia NOA focused on sustainable impact and promoted health and fitness through sport in a project run for over 130 disadvantaged, vulnerable, and refugee children.

Female Olympians in Japan gathered for a programme aimed at tackling gender disparity through capacity building and strengthening of networks of current and future female board members and leaders in sport.

Nepal Olympians Association brought Olympians back to their roots, inspiring students from their rural home districts. Sharing their personal stories pursuing Olympic glory, the Olympians paved the way for future generations to pursue excellence regardless of their background.

For more inspiring stories on how WOA grants and NOA projects made a difference, please check out the Best Practice page on our website. If you would like to submit a Best Practice, please use this submission form.

WOA Service to Society and Service to Olympians grant applications will close on 31 June 2026 at 1700 Lausanne time (CET).

Development Grant applications are also now open for NOAs. NOAs can apply for this $1,000 grant for either or both 2025 and 2026. The funding for the Development Grant is limited and offered to NOAs on a first-come-first-serve basis. If you have any questions please email info@thewoa.org or contact your Development Officer.

title: A message from the WOA President
body:
Dear Members, Dear Fellow Olympians,

I know that we have all been looking forward to the World Olympians Forum in Monaco. Sadly, due to the geopolitical situation in the world right now, we believe it is not the right moment to have you all traveling. Rest assured, we are looking to find a new possibility at a later stage when the conditions are more favourable. 

As Olympians we must stay united and promote peace in the world. You, your NOA and your fellow Olympians, are needed now more than ever. As Olympians we have shown the impact we can have over and over again both on the field of play and in our communities.

Keep focusing on making the world a better place via your local, regional, national and international projects, both personally and through your NOA. We want to hear all about what you are doing. Send your stories to our Development Officers or our CEO and we will continue to publish them on our website and social media. And we look forward to hearing about them in person when we meet at the World Olympians Forum. 

Best Olympian Regards,

Pernilla Wiberg OLY
President

title: Mike Miller to step down as WOA CEO after 14 years
body:
Long-standing WOA CEO Mike Miller will be leaving the organisation at the end of April after 14 years in the job. During his tenure, working closely with WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY, WOA Secretary General Tony Ledgard OLY, WOA Treasurer Patrick Singleton OLY and the WOA Executive Committee, the WOA hugely increased the services and benefits it provides for the worldwide Olympian Community.

During Mike’s time running the operational side of the WOA the WOA created the hugely popular OLY post-nominal letters and OLY Ceremonies, the National Olympians Association’s Grants programmes which fund Service to Society and Service to Olympians projects, the Development Officers who help the NOAs perform to their best, the annual free university scholarships for Olympians, the first-ever Musculo-skeletal survey of retired Olympians and the award-winning OLY House at Rio 2016 and the “best ever” OLY House at Paris 2024.
WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY said: “ Mike has been at the centre of all of our achievements over the past decade and a half. It has been a pleasure to work with him in my roles as WOA Executive Committee Member, WOA Vice-President and now WOA President. We have some big shoes to fill in our search for a new CEO.”

Former WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “When I was elected President the first thing I did was approach Mike whom I knew as a colleague (former IRB Secretary General) as I knew we were aligned on values. I asked him to help me in my mission to reform the WOA and build its strength and capacity. As soon as he accepted the job, working with passion and intelligence, I knew that success would come. When we started there was virtually nothing. Working together and with Tony, Patrick and EXCO, we created so much. I am proud of what we have achieved. Mike has since become a great friend. I wish him well in his future endeavours.”

WOA current and former staff said: “Mike has always shown immense trust in his team, giving us the confidence and space to grow not only professionally, but also as people. He encouraged us to be creative and resourceful, often turning limited means into meaningful outcomes, while empowering us to take ownership and show leadership.

“He combined this with a great sense of humour and a genuine openness to feedback, while always bringing a sharp editorial eye to everything we produced. Working with Mike has been a truly enriching experience, and his impact on the team will be felt for years to come.”

Mike said: “It has been an honour and a privilege to work for the WOA, to work with Olympians from all over the world, and to do my small part in helping to make the world a better place through the values and the spirit of the Olympic Movement.

“There are many people I would like to thank for their invaluable support and friendship over the years. I don’t have enough space to thank you all here personally but there are a few I must mention. Joël, Tony, Patrick, Rebecca, Amaranta, Ayako, Inés, Jovina, Marie-Eve, Myra, Sandrine, Vivian and more recently Pernilla, Lumi and Thomas. Thank-you, thank-you, thank-you. I would also like to thank the three IOC Sports Directors I have worked closely with over the years: Christophe Dubi, Kit McConnell and Pierre Ducrey.

“ With a new President, Secretary General, Treasurer and Executive Committee and after 14 successful years, it’s time to move on. I wish the next CEO all the best and will be there to give advice or any help if needed.  The platform is there for you to carry on building the strength and capacity of the WOA. I’m looking forward to seeing how the WOA evolves over the next 14 years.”

title: Join the 2026 #WhiteCard For Them campaign
body:
Help bring peace to the world and support children’s rights by joining in the Peace and Sport’s #WhiteCard 2026 campaign on April 6, the International Day of Sport for Development and Peace. For over a decade, the #WhiteCard has been a global symbol promoting peace, inclusion, and hope through sport.

This year’s theme, “For them, raise your #WhiteCard,” highlights the urgent need to protect children’s access to safe sport. Around the world, many children grow up facing conflict, exclusion, and disrupted education, missing key life skills such as empathy, cooperation, and resilience that sport helps develop.

Raising a #WhiteCard is a simple but powerful act that shows your commitment to:

  • Children’s rights
  • Access to inclusive sport
  • Peacebuilding in communities

It’s easy for you, your NOA and others to take part. Ask your fellow Olympians to act as ambassadors, visit local communities, and share messages of peace.

It’s simple. All you need to do is get a blank white piece of paper, take a photo, selfie or video and post it on April 6 with the tags #WhiteCard and #IDSDP. You can find more information HERE. And the official campaign toolkit is HERE.

So, raise your card and show the world that Olympians support this important cause.

title: WOA Scholarship changed my life by Ganzi Mugula, Uganda NOA President
body:
When I received the news that I had been awarded a full Scholarship by the World Olympians Association in conjunction with the World Academy of Sport to pursue the Postgraduate Certificate in International Sports Management at the University of London, I knew I had been given an extraordinary opportunity. What I did not anticipate was just how profoundly the experience would shape me—academically, professionally, and personally.

The journey was not without its challenges. Balancing the demands of the programme alongside my daily responsibilities required discipline and sacrifice. During the daytime, I studied in the hours I could squeeze in between working from home. When the day was done and the house grew quiet, I often found myself studying after midnight, sometimes until 1 or 2 a.m., on weekdays. Yet, every late night and every stolen moment of study was worth it. I completed the programme with a distinction grade, an achievement I carry with pride, but the true reward lies in the transformation I experienced along the way.

The programme was enriching. It challenged me to think critically about global issues that shape the world of sport, pushing me to interrogate long-held assumptions and engage deeply with perspectives I had not previously considered. One of the most meaningful dimensions of the experience was the deliberate and thoughtful engagement with decolonizing the subject matter—a process that has fundamentally shifted how I understand international sports management and my role within it.

The course was structured around four modules, with two compulsory units: Financial Management and Sports Strategy, Governance & Leadership. For my electives, I chose Sports Event Management and International Sport Development. Each module offered something unique, but I must admit that Financial Management stood out for me—perhaps because of its mathematical nature, which resonated with my background as a mathematician and computer scientist. There was a comfort in the numbers, but beyond that, the module gave me practical tools that I know will serve me well.

The Governance and Sports Event Management modules were equally rewarding. They were not only engaging but also highly applicable, offering insights that seamlessly bridge local and global sports ecosystems. Whether examining governance structures that shape national federations or dissecting the intricacies of delivering major sporting events, I found myself constantly drawing connections between the course content and the realities I see around me.

I am deeply grateful to the World Olympians Association and the World Academy of Sport for believing in me and investing in my growth. This scholarship has done more than advance my education—it has broadened my perspective, deepened my commitment to the world of sport, and equipped me with the knowledge and confidence to contribute meaningfully to the Olympic movement and beyond.

To any Olympian considering a similar path, I say this: the journey may require sacrifice, but the rewards are immeasurable. This experience has left an indelible mark on my life, and I will carry its lessons with me always.

Note: The WOA would like to thank the World Academy of Sport and the University of London for their continued support of Olympians, helping with their educational and professional growth in a real and meaningful way, as demonstrated by Ganzi’s letter above. This year’s scholarship applications will open in May. Stay tuned to our website and social media.

title: WOA elects two new Vice-Presidents
body:
Following on from the WOA’s recent election the newly constituted WOA Executive Committee (EXCO) has elected Igor Boraska OLY from Croatia and Rosa Rakotozafy OLY of Madagascar as Vice-Presidents.

After each general election the WOA Executive Committee elects two Vice-Presidents from among its members elected by their Continental Grouping. Igor and Rosa replace Pernilla Wiberg OLY, now the WOA President and Mikako Kotani OLY, who did not stand for re-election to the WOA Executive Committee.

WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY said: “We wanted to have a combination of experience, fresh eyes and gender balance. Igor has served with distinction on the WOA Executive Committee and Rosa, as a new member of EXCO, can look with a fresh perspective at how we operate.

“Rosa becomes our first Vice-President from Africa underlining the growth of the WOA in that continent and the importance we place on ensuring diverse voices are heard as we formulate policy and review our actions.”

Rosa Rakotozafy OLY said: “I was delighted to be elected as the female representative on EXCO from Africa. This is an additional honour. I will work closely with the other EXCO members to help build the capacity of the WOA and our National Olympians Associations.”

Igor Boraska OLY said: “Having a blend of experience and new perspectives is so important for any organisation. I’m happy that I will be able to continue to support the good work of the WOA as we seek to continue to improve our services to Olympians to enable them to serve the needs of their communities through the power of sport and the Olympic ideals.”

title: Arrivederci da OLY House Hub Milano e un grande grazie
body:
We hope you all had a great time either in Italy or at home watching the Games. We really enjoyed it here at the OLY House Hub, in Cortina and at Casa Corona.

You made the Games special for us so thank you to all of you who came here or took part in the Games with us online.

And in particular.

Thank you to everyone who came to the OLY House Hub in Milan and chatted with us and told us about your Olympic journeys and the finer points of your sports. We now understand the nuances of the chess on ice sport of Curling, the scoring system of Figure Skating and the different ways Olympians prepare mentally before performing at the highest level.

Thanks to those who signed the Olympians Wall and took Selfies with the Torch here at the Hub.

And we had a huge response to our AI powered online Olympic Torch selfie offer which turned a normal photo into a photo of the Olympian holding the Milano Cortina Olympic Torch. The thank-you emails have been heartwarming. Here are just three of them. “You made my day”, “Wow, many thanks, that brought a tear to my eye” and  “This is perfect, thanks so much.” We will definitely do this again in LA.

And a big shout out to those who wrote inspiring messages on the poster which is being donated to the Vittore Buzzi Children’s Hospital in Milan, who are supported by our kind hosts here in Milan at the Monumentale metro station, the M5 Metro line.

We had so much fun with those who came to the Opening Ceremony Party at Casa Corona and the WOA Party in the Mountains at Slovenia House Cortina, thanks to the Slovenia NOC and NOA. Good food, good drink, good people and good times.

There were 30 OLY@8 shows hosted by our own Development Officer Sandrine Billiet OLY. We learned so much and were inspired by her Olympian guests on each show. So thank you to all those who took part and those who watched in on the e-OLY House Spatial chat platform.

Over 670 Olympians have left their mark online so far on Leave Your Mark and will receive their exclusive Olympians-only commemorative poster after the Games which has the design made up from all the signatures of the Olympians who took part. It’s not too late for you to join in HERE.

So thanks again to you all. Or as we’ve learned to say: grazie mille a tutti voi. See you in two years in LA if not before. Ciao.

title: Olympians in Milan send inspiring words to Children’s Hospital
body:
Olympians who came to the OLY House Hub during Milano-Cortina 2026 all wrote encouraging words on a big poster which will be put on display after the Games at a hospital for children in Milan.

The initiative came about because the venue for the OLY House Hub at the Monumentale Station was generously provided to the WOA by the M5 Metro Line, the sports line. And M5, as part of its community outreach, supports the Vittore Buzzi Children’s Hospital which is at the Gerusalemme Metro Station on the M5 line.

These are some of the words of encouragement, which were in 14 languages.

“Siempre Fuertes” (always strong)

“Dream Big”

“We are cheering for you”

“The Olympic Spirit is with you all”

“You are the architect of your destiny”

“Ciao a tutti. i ragazzi/e, mai mollare. un abbraccio” (Hello, everyone. Never give up guys. Hugs).

There will be a special unveiling ceremony involving Metro 5, the WOA and the Hospital in one of the wards after the Games.

A huge thanks to all the Olympians who took part.

title: WOA Party in the Mountains at Slovenia House Cortina a big hit
body:
The WOA had another great night during the Olympics at Slovenia House, this time in Cortina following in the footsteps of the wonderful party at Slovenia House at PyeongChang 2018

The Olympians who made it through the heavy snowfall enjoyed the finest Slovenian hospitality with traditional dishes and drinks being served. Of course there was music too.

No International Sporting event would be complete without a few speeches. So, the evening kicked off in style with brief but passionate words from WOA Patron HSH Prince Albert II of Monaco OLY, WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY, President of the Club of Slovenian Olympians Iztok Cop OLY and Slovenia Olympic Committee President Franjo Bobinac.

Their messages all keyed in on the power of the Olympic Movement to bring people together and the important role Olympians play in spreading the Olympic values in their communities.

Speeches done, Olympians from all five continents got down to the serious business of chatting, eating, drinking and a few even indulged in a bit of dancing.

So, a big thank you once again (or in our host’s language: še enkrat velika hvala) to the Slovenia NOC and NOA for hosting the WOA and the Olympian community. Their kindness and generosity exemplifies the Olympic Spirit to a T.

title: Catch OLY@8 before it’s too late
body:
If you want to be inspired, informed and entertained don’t miss OLY@8 every day during the Games at 0800 and 2000 cet . But hurry, there are only 5 shows left.

A special Olympian guest joins the WOA’s own Sandrine Billiet OLY to discuss the day’s events, the tactics and strategies of their sport and their Olympian journey from hopeful to Olympian and then to life after competitive sport.

There have been lots of insights and interesting stories. A few examples.

This Morning legendary GB figure skater Robin Cousins OLY,  Gold medallist at Lake Placid in 1980, talked about the Games-time experience. About how for some it was to learn to be more competitive the next time. For some, to do their personal best. And for some to get on the podium. But whatever their aims, he said, you must never forget why you put on your skates the first time and enjoy the experience.

Charlotte Kalla OLY Sweden Cross Country Skiing said that over the years her focus shifted in her career from competing with others more and more to competing with herself. With building her mental strength.

Chris Stokes OLY Jamaica explained how he and his Jamaican bobsleigh teammates had to keep going when everyone was saying they shouldn’t be there, they didn’t belong, they would embarrass themselves and the sport. But the opposite happened,  they grew the sport to new countries and new fans thanks to their perseverance, their hard work and the film Cool Runnings.

Akwasi Frimpong OLY Ghana was the first black male athlete in the world to compete at the Winter Olympics in Skeleton. He said his grandmother told him that: “What you need for success is already within you.” And he is using his Olympian status to show children that they have success within them. Hs foundation, Hope of a Billion, empowers children to make their dreams a reality through workshops and connections. You can find out more about Hope of a Billion HERE.

Sandrine Ray OLY of Switzerland told our Sandrine about the long struggle to have women’s ice hockey accepted by what was a very male dominated sport. She started playing on boy’s teams and had to prove that she was not only as good as the boys, but better. And finally, women’s ice hockey teams were formed in her area and eventually women’s ice hockey made it to the Olympic programme.

With more great guests to come, join Sandrine Billiet OLY at 0800 and 2000 cet through Saturday on OLY@8. Click HERE.

title: Come sign the Olympians Wall at OLY House Hub Milan
body:
Calling all Olympians who will be in Milan for the Olympics. You can join other Olympians by signing the Olympians Wall at the OLY House Hub. At each edition of the Games, the Olympians Wall is where and Olympian can sign by the poster of the Games they competed in and take a photo to be part of the Games forever. It’s a great memory.

In Milan we have all the Winter Olympics posters dating back to the 1956 Games in Milano-Cortina. You can sign on or around the poster in whatever colour pen strikes your fancy. And it’s not just for Winter Olympians, Summer Olympians can come and sign too. We’re one big happy family.

The first Olympian to sign in Milan was Swiss ice hockey Olympian Sandrine Ray who participated in the 2006 Games in Turino. She was swiftly followed by weightlifter Cara Heads Slaughter who competed at Sydney 2000  and is now a trainer. The third Olympians Wall signer was WOA Olympians for Life Simidele Adeagbo OLY of Nigeria, Africa’s first female skeleton Olympian.

At the Hub you can meet your fellow Olympians when you are on your way to or from Olympic events in Milan or when you have a few minutes to spare and are feeling sociable.

You can also get your OLY pin, take a selfie at the selfie wall and sit and chat with other Olympians while watching the day’s action from the Games and having a cup of tea or coffee and something to nibble on.

It’s a cozy space (ok, a small space) so you may have to wait to gain entry at busy times.

The OLY House Hub is located by the ticket gates in the Monumentale Metro station on the Metro 5 Line, the purple one. Come downstairs and inside from any entrance and you can’t miss us.

The OLY House Hub is open from 1100-1800 every day.

Come and join us. Let’s enjoy the Games together.

title: Olympians enjoy the Opening Ceremony at the WOA Watch Parties
body:
The Milano-Cortina Olympic Games kicked off in style at the San Siro watched by Olympians in Milan who weren’t at the stadium at the WOA’s Watch Party at Casa Corona and online at e-OLY House.

The WOA Watch Parties were the place where Olympians from around the world could watch the Opening Ceremony together while reconnecting with old friends or making new friends over a beer or two, or online with a virtual drink.

The Party at Casa Corona was oversubscribed with Olympians coming from far and wide. One Olympian drove 6 hours from Germany just to be at the party. And an Olympian Grandpa was there to see his two Olympian grandchildren as they marched in the Opening Ceremony.

Also in attendance were an Olympian for Life inductee, the President of one of the WOA’s newest National Olympians Association and a family who came all the way from the South Pacific, for the Games, not just for the party.

e-OLY House opened its doors for the Opening Ceremony with the platform hosted by the WOA’s Sandrine Billiet OLY. WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY gave a short welcome speech and then attendees watched the Ceremony and chatted amongst themselves.

There will be a WOA party in Cortina, details to be announced soon.

And OLY@8 starts today (Saturday). Every day during the Games Sandrine will be joined by an Olympian guest to preview the days events at 8am cet and to review the days events at 8pm cet at e-OLY House. You can enter e-OLY House 24/7 HERE.

title: Leave your Mark is back for Milano-Cortina
body:
Whether you are in Milan or Cortina or not, you can be a part of the Olympic Games in Milano-Cortina 2026 forever. How? Simply by joining Olympians from all over the world to Leave your Mark.

Add your name, your autograph and the hometown you want to show on the Leave your Mark map. We had over 2,000 Olympians who left their mark in the Paris 2024 and Beijing 2022 editions. It’s quick and easy to Leave your Mark on our online platform HERE. 

After the Games, you will receive an exclusive downloadable souvenir poster created from the marks collected by all Olympians as a permanent memory of your contribution to the Olympic Games Milano-Cortina 2026.

And there’s more you can do to join in the Games experience without coming to Milan or Cortina. Join your fellow Olympians at e-OLY House, your home at home for the Games. There you can with other Olympians and take part in lots of interesting activities.

Find out about everything that is happening at the OLY House Hub in Milan and e-OLY House HERE.

title: Take part in Milano-Cortina wherever you are at e-OLY House
body:
Join your Olympian friends around the world during the Olympic Games at e-OLY House which opens Friday evening (February 6th). There’s lots going on, starting with the Olympic Games Opening Ceremony. Watch the Ceremony and chat live with your friends. Doors open at 1900 cet. There’ll be a short hello from WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY at around 1930 cet and then it’s Opening Ceremony time.

Every day there’s OLY@8. Each morning at 0800 cet and each evening at 2000 cet (8pm) our own Sandrine Billiet OLY will be joined by a special guest to preview and review the day’s events and delve into the memory locker.

You, as an Olympian, can enter e-OLY House at any time to chat with whoever is there or bring your family and friends while you are there. There’s lots of stuff to look at and there will be some fun parties and games too.

e-OLY House is based on the SpatialChat platform where you are an avatar that can move about and behave just as if you were at a party or a conference, you hear people close to you and as you move away you hear those you move next to. There’s a stage where OLY@8 will be presented and different rooms with different activities. It’s best experienced on a laptop.

So, jump right in and be part of Milano-Cortina 2026. Ski wear optional.

Enter through the OLY House website. https://www.olyhouse.org.

See you during the Games.

The WOA Team

title: WOA elects first ever female President
body:
In a day of firsts, the WOA General Assembly yesterday elected double Olympic Champion Pernilla Wiberg OLY of Sweden its first ever female President, echoing the election of Kirsty Coventry as the IOC’s first ever female President.

Former Alpine Skiing World Champion and Olympic Gold Medallist Pernilla Wiberg OLY has vast experience within the Olympic Movement. She was an IOC Member, a member of the IOC Athletes’ Commission, a WOA Executive Committee Member and was one of the WOA’s two Vice-Presidents until her election as President.

The WOA also elected its first ever Secretary General from Africa, Olumide Oyedeji OLY of Nigeria and its first ever Asian Treasurer, Thomas Tang OLY of Chinese Taipei. The newly elected Executive Committee contains members from all five continents and is gender balanced, with two representatives from each continent, one male and one female.

WOA President Pernilla Wiberg OLY said: “l would like to thank the Olympians of the world for bestowing this great honour on me. Becoming the fifth WOA President is very special, and being the first ever female in the post makes it even more special. I would like to thank the other presidential candidates, James Tomkins OLY and German Glessner OLY, for their part in the WOA’s democratic election process.

“The composition of the WOA leadership represents the diversity and the inclusiveness of the Olympic Movement. We will strive to ensure that the core founding values of the Olympics are always at the heart of the Olympic Movement along with the needs and aspirations of the Olympians themselves.

“I am looking forward to working closely with IOC President Kirsty Coventry and her team. Together we can keep the Olympic flame burning bright and make a real contribution to our regions, our nations and our local communities. There are already many Olympians acting as positive role models in society. The Olympic Movement, working as one, can help make the world a better, healthier, more inclusive and more active place.”

Outgoing WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said; “It has been an honour and a privilege  to serve as the WOA President these past 15 years. Together we built the capacity of the WOA and the National Olympians Associations, running award-winning OLY Houses, creating the OLY post-nominal letters for Olympians, starting the Service to Olympians and Service to Society grants programmes and organising three great World Olympians Forums in Moscow, Lausanne and Istanbul.

“I would like to thank everyone who has been on this great journey with us. We leave a very solid base for Pernilla and her team to build on. She is absolutely the best person to take the WOA and the National Olympians Associations to new heights. I wish her and the newly elected Executive Committee well and ask them when making decisions to  always be guided by our motto: Service to Olympians, Service to Society. By serving the needs of Olympians we can empower them to serve the needs of Society. That’s what the modern Olympic Movement was founded to do.”

The full list of those elected to the WOA Executive Committee is:

President 
Pernilla Wiberg (Sweden)

Secretary General 
Olumide Oyedeji (Nigeria)

Treasurer 
Wei-Tsu (Thomas) Tang (Chinese Taipei)

EXCO Members Africa 
Rosa Rakotozafy (Madagascar)
Andrew Owusu (Ghana)

EXCO Members Americas 
Claire Carver-Dias (Canada)
Willie Banks (USA)

EXCO Members Asia 
Gillian Akiko Thomson Guevara (Philippines)
Deepak Bista (Nepal)

EXCO Members Europe 
Stavroula Kozompoli (Greece)
Igor Boraska (Croatia)

EXCO Members Oceania 
Julia Bell (Australia)
Carl Probert (Fiji)

title: IOC and WOA issue Joint Declaration
body:
We are very pleased to announce that we have agreed a Joint Declaration with the IOC that spells out the key points of our recently signed agreement and the benefits arising from that for National Olympians Associations and Olympians.

The Declaration demonstrates the close relationship between our two organisations and our mutual desire to ensure that the needs of Olympians are met and the National Olympians Associations are given the tools they need to be as strong as they can be for the benefit of their members and society at large.

As the Declaration states: “IOC and WOA will work closely together to support NOAs and help them engage and empower Olympians to foster Olympism in their communities.”

The Declaration also re-affirms the IOC’s commitment to support the WOA going forward in a number of ways including financially. And it re-affirms the WOA’s commitment to continue to comply with the Olympic Charter, and the IOC Code of Ethics, including the Basic Universal Principles of Good Governance within the Olympic Movement.

The IOC will be promoting OLY sign-ups in the Olympic Villages at the Milan-Cortina Games, as they have done at past Games. And the IOC will be represented at the upcoming WOA General Assembly and World Olympians Forum. WOA will be promoting the various IOC Athlete365 initiatives and services for Olympians, as we did at OLY House Paris 2024.

title: Here’s to a great 2026
body:
Happy New Year everyone,

2025 was, let’s call it, a mixed year with highs and lows, difficulties and successes and quite a few changes. Thank you all for your patience and understanding as we navigated all that the year threw at us. During 2025 we worked very hard to preserve our independence as democratically decided by you. Being independent is not incompatible with having a good, close working relationship with the IOC, which we now have again and which we have had for most of our existence.

That was 2025. For 2026, there is so much to look forward to.

The General Assembly on January 18th will give us a chance to all gather together to look back at the achievements of the past four years and to look forward to LA 2028. And a new President, Secretary General and Treasurer will be elected along with a new Executive Committee. I wish all the candidates the best of luck and will be there to help out, if requested, once my term of office ends at the close of the General Assembly.

Then there is the Winter Olympics in Milano-Cortina in February. The Games are what it is all about for us Olympians. New stars, new records, new friendships and of course, new OLYs. We will unveil the WOA activities during the Games soon. If you would like to host an online party during Milano-Cortina on our e-OLY House platform please contact the team at info@thewoa.org.

April will see the World Olympians Forum in-person in Monaco. The Istanbul edition will be a hard act to follow but I’m sure Monaco with its long history of hosting international events will be up to the task. The Forum is always a great place to share best practices, hear from experts and for us all to network and strengthen the Olympian community.

And in October and November there’s the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. This will be an historic event as it is the first Olympic Games of any sort to be held in Africa. The YOG is the future of our Movement and usually produces some great sport, so don’t miss it. I would like to congratulate our Executive Committee member and former WOA Vice-President Amadou Dia Ba OLY for his role in helping secure the Games for Senegal and helping bring them to fruition.

Finally, a plea. You will recall that we asked you to help Jamaican Olympians rebuild after the hurricane. You have been generous so far. But they still need just over one thousand dollars to reach their target. Let’s kick-off 2026 by helping our fellow Olympians in Jamaica celebrate the new year in style. https://olympians.org/news/1951/help-jamaican-olympians-rebuild-after-the-hurricane/

Best Olympian regards to you and your families and friends for 2026.

Joël

title: Help Jamaican Olympians rebuild after the hurricane
body:
Jamaican Olympians are reaching out to the worldwide Olympian community to help them rebuild a much-loved sports facility severely damaged by Hurricane Melissa. For generations, St. Elizabeth Technical High School (STETHS) has been more than just a school; it has been a home, a pathway to success, and a place where young people learn to dream bigger—both academically and athletically. The school has produced world-class athletes, Olympians, and future leaders.

With the girls' dormitories in urgent need of repair, the National Association of Jamaican Olympians (NAJO) is calling on you to help rebuild STETHS and support the next generation of student-athletes.

All funds raised through the GoFundMe project will be dedicated solely to restoring the roof of the girls’ dormitory at St. Elizabeth Technical High School. The National Association of Jamaican Olympians will oversee the management of these funds to ensure transparency and accountability.

Cathy Rattray OLY, NAJO Secretary said: “Hurricane Melissa left significant damage in its wake, and St. Elizabeth Technical High School—one of Jamaica’s most respected institutions—was among the hardest hit. Young Jamaican female athletes depend on this safe, stable living environment to continue their education and athletic training. Quickly restoring STETHS will ensure continuity and give them hope for the future.”

Dr. Neil Gardner OLY, NAJO President said: “St. Elizabeth Technical High School holds a special place in Jamaica’s sporting history. For generations it has nurtured discipline, resilience, and excellence—values that shaped many of Jamaica’s Olympians long before they wore national colours. STETHS was not only where athletic talent was developed, but where character was formed, dreams were encouraged, and lifelong lessons were learned. Any donation you can give, no matter how small, will help these young athletes fulfil their Olympic and life dreams.”

You can donate here. https://bit.ly/4aq3Ux3

title: IOC and WOA strengthen their partnership to better support Olympians
body:
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) and the World Olympians Association (WOA) will further increase their joint support for Olympians. The two organisations have just renewed their partnership by signing a new Cooperation and Licence Agreement.

Building on the IOC’s longstanding support of the WOA, the Agreement is aimed at:

  • enhancing the engagement and support for Olympians
  • strengthening the collaboration between the two organisations; and
  • strengthening the good governance which underpins the partnership.

The Agreement also focuses on maximising the impact of joint initiatives and resources to ensure that Olympians continue to be empowered to serve as role models and ambassadors of the Olympic Movement.

IOC President and Double Olympic Champion Kirsty Coventry said: “As Olympians, we share a lifelong bond through the values and experiences that define the Olympic Movement. This renewed partnership between the IOC and the WOA strengthens our collective commitment to support Olympians — not only during their sporting careers but throughout their lives. Together, we will continue to empower Olympians as role models, community leaders and ambassadors of the Olympic ideals around the world.”

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY,  Olympic bronze medallist and World Champion, said: “We are delighted that our relationship with the IOC is being strengthened so that we can best serve the needs of our National Associations and individual Olympians with more resources and more support from the IOC.  We have achieved much over the last three Olympic cycles, including the creation of the OLY post-nominal letters and our grants and scholarship programmes, and we look forward to working hand in hand with the IOC to deliver even more services and opportunities for Olympians. ”

About the WOA

The IOC has supported the World Olympians Association since its foundation, which was led by former IOC President Juan Antonio Samaranch in 1995.

The WOA supports Olympians worldwide and helps over 100 National Olympians Associations spread the spirit of Olympism in their country. It unites Olympians from all Games and generations, empowering them to make the world a better place through the values of sport.

For more information, visit olympians.org.

title: IOC and WOA to reaffirm commitment to work closely together
body:
The following is a joint communication from the IOC and the WOA.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) and World Olympians Association (WOA) have held a series of constructive meetings over the past few weeks aimed at deepening their relationship and increasing support and benefits for Olympians all over the world. The two organisations have agreed to develop a new Memorandum of Understanding which will guide their working relationship going forward.

IOC Director General Christophe De Kepper said: “The WOA, its National Associations and Olympians are important ambassadors of the Olympic Movement. By working closely together with the WOA we can ensure that Olympians are properly supported.”

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “Only by working in harmony with the IOC can we provide the best possible service to our National Associations and to Olympians through all stages of their lives. The deepened relationship with the IOC will help us ensure Olympians are at the heart of the Olympic Movement and that their needs and aspirations are properly catered for by both us and the IOC. We are very appreciative of the support of the IOC.”

A working group composed of IOC and WOA representatives has been established to develop the MOU ahead of the next General Assembly of the World Olympians Association at the end of November in Monaco.

title: Olympians in action on Olympic Day
body:
Olympians around the world engaged with their communities on Olympic Day to spread the values of the Olympic Movement and the joy of taking part in sport. Their National Olympians Associations worked with their National Olympic Committees, Athletes Commissions and other sports organisations to run lots of projects. Here are a few of their stories.

In New Zealand there was a sustainability twist to the day. Olympians shared their inspirational stories before they and children from a local school planted 1,375 trees to help rehabilitate a local waterway.

The theme in Japan was “Let’s Move”. And move the members of the Japan Olympians Association certainly did.

460 students and teachers attended the “Be the Next Olympian” programme in Malaysia. The programme, run by the Olympians Association, spells out what the Olympics values brings to peoples’ lives and teaches the importance of safe sports. The highlight of the day was a sharing session with Olympians and former national athletes. https://www.instagram.com/p/DLRw5DcPAsv/

The Hellenic Olympians Association along with the International Olympic Truce Centre hosted a special event at the Olympic Museum of Athens where children aged 5 to 12 got to try out different sports and take part in a discussion on the Olympic Truce and the values of sport.

The Philippine Olympians ran an Olympians Sports Leadership Programme on Olympic Day. The pillars of  programme , Storytelling, Networking and Systems Thinking, beautifully dovetail with the Olympic values. Excellence in the stories we believe and tell; Friendship in the people we engage and network with; Fair Play in the work we pursue individually and collectively. You can learn more about the Philippine OSLP programme at https://oslp.adrenaline.solutions/.

The Irish, of course, celebrated with the craic (which means a good, fun time). Irish Olympians spanning six decades came together for an inaugural Olympic Day BBQ along with their families, friends, and staff from the Olympic Federation of Ireland (OFI). A brand-new Olympians’ signing wall was unveiled at Olympic House, a tribute to the athletes who have represented Ireland on the world stage. Each Olympian present received an OLY pin, marking their special place within the global Olympic community.

In Australia, WOA Executive Committee Member Nat Cook went to Chapel Hill State School in Brisbane to talk sport and the power of sport to unite the world. About how sport is a language everyone speaks. And how everyone can dream big just like the athletes. And with Brisbane 2032 coming they were really excited, as you can see in this short video.

In India, Olympic Day at Reliance Foundation School brought champions, children, and Olympic values together. https://www.instagram.com/reel/DLP59RQTQB3/

On Olympic Day, the Angolan Olympic and Paralympic Athletes Association held an event where athletes shared their stories, talked about the Olympic Pillars and Values, and promoted health and fitness. You can see lots about the day at https://www.facebook.com/share/v/16QA7x3v3F/

The Nepal Olympians Association, working with their NOC, ran their School to Olympic Programme to encourage school children to take part in sport.

There was also a celebration in Kathmandu at the renowned UNESCO World Heritage Soyambhu Temple.

Mauritian Olympians joined the students of the Mauritius Academy of Sport programme to share their journey, values, and love for sport. Students of the programme had the chance to engage in practical workshops and open discussions around the Olympic values of respect, excellence, and fair play.
