title: Monaco to host World Olympians Forum
body:
The fourth World Olympians Association’s World Olympians Forum (WOF) will be held in Monaco in the beginning of September in conjunction with the WOA General Assembly. The one-day WOF will be on Tuesday September 2 and the General Assembly on Wednesday September 3. The 150 attendees will arrive on September 1 and depart on September 4.

Previous World Olympians Forums were held in Moscow in 2015, in Lausanne in 2019 and in Istanbul in 2023. This year’s World Olympians Forum will be streamed live as was successfully done in Istanbul two years ago. The Forum will once again be the place where the WOA’s 111 National Associations share best practices and inspirational stories, hear from world renowned experts and government officials on sports management, projects for the social good, health, governance and safety and take part in workshops to enhance their skills and build their connections with each other.

The WOA General Assembly will look back at the last four years and ahead to the next four up to the LA 2028 Olympic Games. The WOA President, Secretary General and Treasurer will be directly elected by all the delegates at the General Assembly and each of the five Continental Groupings of National Olympians Associations will elect two Executive Committee representatives, one male and one female.

The events, which were expected to be held in Taipei, have been relocated to Monaco for operational reasons.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “We are very grateful to our Patron, HSH Prince Albert II of Monaco, for his show of support for the WOA by giving us the opportunity to host these two very important events in the principality of Monaco. Monaco is one of the world leading centres for international prestige events such as the Monaco Grand Prix, the Monte Carlo Television Festival and Sportel Monaco. 

“The previous three World Olympians Forums have been exceptional as our National Olympians Associations shared their best practices and projects, gained knowledge imparted from the expert speakers, and built connections through the discussions, workshops and cultural events at the Forum. The WOA General Assembly, held after every summer edition of the Olympic Games, is where our members have their say on the future direction of the WOA and the programmes, projects and services we provide for them and for all Olympians.”

title: Apply now for University of London scholarships
body:
Applications are now open for four full scholarships offered through WOA to Olympians to further their study online at the prestigious University of London (UoL).

The Postgraduate Certificate in International Sports Management accelerates careers in the sports industry as a globally recognised university qualification. In addition to the full scholarships, there will be thirty partial funding offers available to Olympians who enroll in the programme.

The course is time-flexible, remote and self-paced. It is ideal for Olympians at every stage of their careers, with intake options in September 2025 and February 2026. For more information about the course, including entry requirements, click here.

Applications for the scholarship will close on 15 July 2025. To apply, fill in the application form here.

The scholarship initiative between WOA, World Academy of Sport and UoL has been a huge success over the past five years. Over 60 Olympians have completed the programme since its launch in 2020.

title: Read the letter from the WOA Officers to NOAs, NOCs and IOC Members
body:
The WOA Officers, the President, Secretary General and Treasurer, have sent an email with a letter attached to National Olympians Associations, National Olympic Committees and IOC Members. The wording of the email is below and the link to the letter attached is HERE. 

Dear National Olympians Associations, National Olympic Committees and IOC Members,

Please find attached our response to the recent communications to you from the International Olympic Committee.

Our aim is to clarify facts, reaffirm our commitment to the Olympic Movement, and respectfully address concerns raised. We remain dedicated to constructive engagement, mutual respect, and our shared Olympic values. We believe in respecting democratic processes as fundamental to our unity and integrity.

We hope our attached letter fosters a more open and informed dialogue moving forward.

Thank you for your kind attention to this.

Best Olympian Regards,

Joël Bouzou OLY, WOA President
Anthony Ledgard OLY, WOA Secretary General
Patrick Singleton OLY, WOA Treasurer

title: Another 5 years of clean financial audits for WOA
body:
The World Olympians Association has just shared the recently completed audit report of its financial statements for 2023 by PwC in Switzerland with its member National Olympians Associations (NOAs), marking another five years of clean audits in a sequence that now stretches back more than a decade.

The audit reports are shared with NOAs as they are finalised and then presented to the WOA General Assembly every four years.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “Our financial processes are robust and our annual financial statements are accurate as validated by PwC, one of the world’s “Big Four” accounting firms. I would like to thank our Treasurer, our administration staff and our external accountant for their diligence and hard work on this over the years.”

WOA Treasurer Patrick Singleton OLY said: “We have very strong controls in place. For instance, four separate signatures are needed before any payment can be made. Our highly experienced Swiss external accountant runs our accounting function. And when specific specialised tax or other advice is needed, we enlist the help of top Swiss or International legal or accounting companies.”

WOA Secretary General Anthony Ledgard OLY said: “We always share our annual financial information with our members, the 111 National Olympians Associations, in accordance with our constitution. We are looking forward to meeting them in person at our next General Assembly in September and answering any questions they may have.”

You can access the WOA Financial Audit Reports 2019-2023 HERE. The 2024 Financial Audit Report will be sent to our members as soon as it is finalised.

title: Shape the Future of Support for Olympians
body:
As the global conversation around athlete compensation evolves, most recently reignited by the introduction of prize money for Athletics gold medallists at Paris 2024, it is more important than ever to better understand how Olympians are supported on their journey to the world’s biggest sporting stage.

In light of this, I am pleased to share an important research initiative led by three postgraduate students from the internationally renowned FIFA Master in Management, Law and Humanities of Sport. Their thesis explores the financial and institutional structures that underpin the Olympic experience, aiming to highlight both the strengths and gaps in athlete support worldwide.

They have prepared a short survey, which will take approximately 10 minutes, to gather insights directly from Olympians like you. Your voice is vital to ensure this research reflects the real experiences and needs of our community. I encourage you to take part.

Please note that this survey is for Olympians aged 18 and over only. All responses will be anonymised. The deadline to complete the survey is 1st June 2025.

https://shout.com/s/olympic-athlete-compensation 

A few words about the researchers:

Phillip Wilson is a two-time Olympian and Tokyo 2020 gold medallist in rowing for New Zealand.

Daniela Huamán, from Peru and the UK via Spain, is transitioning from a decade-long career in marketing, combining her experiences in basketball, football, and running with a belief in sport’s power to create positive social impact.

Simon Grunwerg from the United Kingdom has over 8 years of commercial finance experience in media agencies, and is now transitioning into the sports industry to combine his business expertise with his passion for sport.

If you have any questions about the survey or the research, please feel free to contact the research team directly at athleteresearch.fifamaster@gmail.com.

Thank you in advance for your participation and support of this valuable project.

Best Olympian Regards,

Joël Bouzou OLY
President

title: WOA Congratulates new IOC President Kirsty Coventry on her stunning victory
body:
WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY has sent a note of congratulations to the newly elected IOC President Kirsty Coventry. Kirsty Coventry has become the first female President in the history of the IOC and follows in the footsteps of the previous two Presidents in being an Olympian.

Joël Bouzou OLY said: "We are very proud and happy that an Olympian will be at the helm of the IOC for at least another eight years. A first-round landslide victory was certainly unexpected but shows the unity of thought of the IOC Members. By electing the first female President the IOC Members demonstrated that the years of the IOC, WOA and others working for gender equality have paid off.

“We worked very well with Kirsty when she was Chair of the IOC Athletes’ Commission and are looking forward to working closely with her again to promote the interests of Olympians, the IOC, the Olympic Movement and society in general through the power of Olympism and the role model influence of Olympians.

“We are hoping to meet with Coventry and her team very soon to discuss how we can deepen our relationship and help her achieve her five key priorities as spelled out in her election manifesto, which were to: ‘harness the power of sport, maximize collaboration & engagement, strengthen partnerships for mutual growth, champion sustainable development and advance credibility and trust.’”

title: IOC Presidential Candidates reply to WOA Open Letter
body:
Three candidates of the seven standing to become the next IOC President at Thursday’s election have sent in replies to the Open Letter sent to all the candidates by the WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY.

In his reply, Mr Morinari Watanabe said that “the IOC needs to be a more open organization and that he would like “to increase the presence of sport by strengthening the relationship between the IOC and the IFs, WOA, etc.” He also said he wanted to give Olympians “more opportunities than ever before to get involved and contribute to all phases of the Olympic Games, before, during and after the Games.”

HRH Prince Feisal Al Hussein said that he would “establish workshops for athletes to actively contribute to the development of Olympic Agenda 2036” and that he would “engage our broadcast and commercial partners on how we can help athletes create content around their Olympic experience.” He said that through “open dialogue, and collaboration with our stakeholders, we can collaboratively design a future that better values their voice, their well-being, and their participation, recognising the crucial role they play.”

Lord Sebastian Coe said that “I believe the role of Olympic alumni is extremely important to the Olympic movement” and that the IOC should “create shared-value models where athletes benefit from the Games’ commercial success, recognising them as essential partners.” He also added that he would “ensure athletes have meaningful decision-making representation” within the IOC.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “We are very pleased that the candidates are recognising that the Olympians and the WOA play a crucial role in the Olympic Movement and the work of the IOC. We look forward to working closely with the new IOC President and their team for the benefit of Olympians, the Olympic Movement and society in general.”

As a reminder. the Open Letter from the WOA to the candidates asked the following questions:

  1. How do you intend to ensure that Olympians are truly at the heart of the IOC’s activities
  2. What is your vision for a strong, collaborative, and equitable partnership between our two independent organisations
  3. Would you support initiatives such as free medical screenings and health checks for all competitors before, during, and after the Olympic Games, including free or subsidised medical insurance for life for Olympian
  4. Do you believe Olympians should have the right to use footage of their Olympic performances
  5. What are your views on financial recognition for Olympians’ participation in the Olympic Games

You can see the full replies of Mr Morinari Watanabe, HRH Prince Faisal Al Hussein and Lord Sebastian Coe here.

title: WOA has sent an Open Letter to the IOC Presidential Candidates
body:
With less than a week to go until the IOC Presidential election, the WOA has written to the seven candidates seeking their views on the big issues that affect Olympians and the working of the WOA itself.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “The purpose of the letter is to ask the candidates to expand on the general issues they raised in their election manifestos with regard to Olympians, democracy and working relationships within the Olympic Movement and to see what they will commit to that would benefit Olympians and the work of the WOA in supporting Olympians and promoting the values of the Olympic Movement.

“As I said in the open letter, the WOA, as the independent democratically elected body representing Olympians worldwide, is committed to fostering a constructive and mutually beneficial relationship with the next IOC President and their team. We firmly believe that a partnership founded on respect, collaboration, and a shared commitment to the well-being of Olympians will serve to strengthen the Olympic Movement as a whole.”

The candidates were asked these five questions:

  1. How do you intend to ensure that Olympians are truly at the heart of the IOC’s activities?
  2. What is your vision for a strong, collaborative, and equitable partnership between our two independent organisations?
  3. Would you support initiatives such as free medical screenings and health checks for all competitors before, during, and after the Olympic Games, including free or subsidised medical insurance for life for Olympians?
  4. Do you believe Olympians should have the right to use footage of their Olympic performances?
  5. What are your views on financial recognition for Olympians’ participation in the Olympic Games?

We will publish the replies as we receive them. You can see the full letter here.

title: Female Olympians: Apply now for grants of up to $5,000
body:
For the third year running the SimiSleighs Foundation is providing grants for female Olympians worldwide, empowering them by providing crucial financial support for training, competition, and personal development. The Foundation, led by WOA Olympians for Life awardee Simidele Adeagbo OLY, is once again running its highly popular six-month virtual programme.

The grants are open to female Olympic and Paralympic athletes and hopefuls aiming to represent their countries at the Milano-Cortina 2026 or Los Angeles 2028 Games. With a financial support package of up to $5,000 USD, the grant aims to help athletes cover the expenses associated with high-level training and international competition. The programme also provides valuable personal and professional development opportunities, fostering a sense of community and mentorship among women in sport.

“For many female athletes, the difference between achieving their dreams or not often comes down to access—access to resources, opportunities, and support,” said Simidele Adeagbo OLY, founder of the SimiSleighs Foundation. “This grant is a direct investment in the future of these women. The 2025 cohort will be part of a global movement that is reshaping the landscape for women in sport, and I am honoured to continue to support them on their journeys.”

2024 programme participant Helen Maroulis OLY said, “Throughout my journey, the SimiSleighs Foundation Athlete Grant Programme has been an incredible support. The tools I’ve gained—like personalised nutrition guidance and sports psychology strategies—have helped me maintain balance and stay focused, especially during intense competition. This programme has truly played a key role in my success, both on and off the field." 

To apply, please visit the SimiSleighs Foundation website: www.simisleighsfoundation.org/athlete-grant-program.

title: Say no to GBV
body:
Gender-based violence (GBV) is a huge issue throughout the world. It affects all parts of society in all countries. And Olympians are not immune as we saw after Paris 2024. One in three women worldwide have directly experienced violence. Every 10 minutes, a woman is killed by a partner or family member. These aren't just statistics - our community, our friends, our competitors, are affected. Olympians like Agnes, Rebecca and Damaris. Three exceptional athletes. 

Three lives cut short by gender-based violence.

A new movement called 1in3 has been set up to end this cycle of violence.

Please have a look at their website 1in3.org and join your fellow Olympians in saying no to GBV by signing up here.  

The more Olympians who sign up, the stronger the movement.

It’s time to put an end to GBV. Athletes hold unprecedented influence, representing over 50% of society’s most impactful voices. Take action at 1in3.org so that no woman ever has to fear going home.

Your support is crucial. Thank you.

title: Apply for discounted postgraduate Sports Diplomacy course
body:
Dear Fellow Olympians, 

The Hungarian University of Sports Science is offering one lucky Olympian a massive discount on its postgraduate Sports Diplomacy programme. The one-year hybrid course, which starts in February 2025, consists of two terms with 80% online and two weeks per term in person at its Budapest campus.

The programme is for second career athletes in federations and government and non-government organisations. It mixes online, in-person and internship learnings. And at the end you are awarded a “Sport Diplomacy Specialist” degree

The course normally costs €3,200, but WOA has negotiated a special price of €1,800. You would have to pay your own costs of travel, accommodation and other expenses during your four weeks on campus.

The deadline for Olympian applications is 15 December 2024. More information can be found in the brochure here or by contacting sdp@tf.hu.

The WOA Team

title: WOA awards four more Olympians full postgraduate scholarships
body:
Four Olympians who want to give back to their communities have been awarded the postgraduate scholarship offered by World Academy of Sport and World Olympians Association. They will undertake the University of London’s International Sports Management programme in the academic year 2024/25.

The WOA full scholarship recipients are:

  • Ayonika Paul OLY - India, Shooting
  • Nathalia Siqueira Almeida OLY - Brazil, Aquatics
  • Eldric Sella Rodriguez OLY - Refugee Olympic Team, Boxing
  • Yee Pui Fong OLY - Hong Kong, Athletics

You can still join them with a 25% scholarship from WOA. The postgraduate certificate in International Sport Management programme is delivered online in English and can be completed at your own pace. For the February 2025 intake, scholarship applications are open now till 31 December 2024. Apply HERE

This year’s four awardees strongly stressed their desire to use what they learn on the course to not only improve themselves, but also to improve their communities, their sports and the welfare of their fellow athletes. This is what they had to say:

Ayonika Paul OLY - India, Shooting

“As an elite athlete who has participated in the Olympic Games, I have dedicated my life to excellence in sports. This dedication extends to my education, where I pursued studies at the highest level. My goal is to transition from athlete to a leadership role within the sports industry. I aspire to bring fresh insights and innovative solutions to the sports industry. I aim to influence policy, improve athlete welfare, and promote sports at all levels. I hope to make a meaningful impact and contribute to the future of sports.”

Nathalia Siqueira Almeida OLY - Brazil, Aquatics

“I always knew I wanted more than just being a swimmer. I want to share what the sport has given me with younger generations. In my country, very few people grow to become professional athletes and the lack of a symbiotic relationship between sports and education creates an environment where thousands of kids are left forgotten trying to pursue a career in sports. My dream is to live in a country where kids don’t have to choose between the sport they love and their careers. Being part of this program will give me the tools to help build that path.”

Eldric Sella Rodriguez OLY - Refugee Olympic Team, Boxing

“I believe sports is a great tool for personal development in everybody’s life. With this scholarship, I can get the proper knowledge to be able to work in the sports industry and be able to use sports to help others as it has helped me.”

Yee Pui Fong OLY - Hong Kong, Athletics

“Since 2023, I have been selected to be Hong Kong Representatives Selection Committee of Hong Kong, China Association of Athletics Affiliates, which gave me more opportunities to learn about the operations of a sports association. Balancing the operations and finance with the expectation of the stakeholders has always been a difficult and ever-lasting issue to handle with. In view of such, I am taking the PGc to equipe myself with professional knowledge and subsequently to contribute to the sports field combing with my sports and work experience.

title: Six films chosen for prestigious awards at OLY House Film Festival
body:
Six worthy winners have been announced for the first ever OLY House Film Festival which was held at OLY House Paris 2024 @ Caisse d’Epargne and online at e-OLY House. The films were either made by Olympians or are about the Olympic Movement and the spirit that guides all Olympians.

Twenty-nine films were screened over the 17 days of the Olympic Games in the 96-seat theatre at OLY House and online at e-OLY House. A number of directors and producers, including Olympic Champion Edwin Moses OLY, took part in Q&A sessions after the screening of their films.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “Choosing the winners was very difficult. This was a very strong collection of stories that captured the essence of what it is to be an Olympian and how we, as Olympians, can have a major impact for good in society as role models using the power of sport in all sectors of our communities to inspire others and enhance the lives of those around us.”

The six winners selected by the jury of film producer and president of the European Film Academy Mike Downey OBE, WOA president and 4-time Olympian Joël Bouzou OLY and cinematographer Konstantin Esadze and Olympians themselves are:

Best Feature Film: Moses - 13 Steps (Michael Wech)

MOSES - 13 Steps is a powerful exploration of the life and legacy of Edwin Moses, an unparalleled athlete and visionary whose triumphs on and off the track catalysed significant social and scientific change and inspired generations to break barriers of all kinds.

Best Short Film: Surfing Through the Odds (Ana Filipa Domingues)

In São Tomé and Príncipe, where girls traditionally spend most of their day collecting water and helping their families and were previously not allowed to surf, SOMA fights for gender equality through surf therapy, academic support, and mental health education.

Spirit of Sport Award: A Ball (Octavio Maya)

A humble ball speaks to a rich ball and expresses its deepest thoughts about the real meaning of rolling in life.

Olympic Spirit Award: Samir - The Power of Dreams (Eric Bacos)

Samir - The Power of Dreams tells the story of a Moroccan born in France to a modest family who, through his dreams, made sport history by becoming Morocco's first Winter Olympic athlete.

Special Jury Prize: Strong Grandma (Cecilia Brown & Winslow Crane-Murdoch)

Ninety-five-year-old Catherine Kuehn, a world record-winning powerlifter, reflects on the love and loss that brought her to this moment as she prepares for her last competition.

Olympians Choice Award: He Happened (Dejan Acimovic)

He Happened is the story of Ratko Rudic, one of the greatest water polo coaches of all time, featuring 125 prominent figures in water polo who discuss his career, his bad luck as a player and his numerous gold medals as a coach with three different national teams.

title: We’ll always have Paris
body:
What a Games! So many great moments to savour. At the venues. On tv and social. And at OLY House Paris 2024 @ Caisse d’Epargne and e-OLY House.

The Games were a great success. And so was OLY House.

The Games may be over and OLY House closed, but it’s not all over for Olympians. Olympians, you can keep your memories alive and forever be a part of the Games if you click HERE to Leave your Mark.

No matter where you are from, when you competed or your stage in life, the unique bond we share as Olympians holds our community together.

Leave your Mark to thank all involved in making the Paris Olympic Games a success.

You will receive an exclusive downloadable souvenir poster created from the marks collected which you can print and frame as a permanent memory of your contribution to the Olympic Games Paris 2024.

And you can still check out e-OLY House HERE, the online home at home for Olympians during the Games powered by SpatialChat, featuring Olympian speakers, the OLY House Film Festival films and so much more. It’s open until August 19th. The password is eolyhouse2024.

Thanks to you all for your part in making the Olympic Games Paris 2024 and OLY House so special. See you in Milano-Cortina 2026 and LA 2028.

title: Edwin Moses OLY film has European Premiere at OLY House
body:
The OLY House Paris 2024 Theatre was full for a private screening of the Edwin Moses OLY documentary Moses - 13 Steps. The film shows the life of Edwin Moses OLY both as an athlete who was undefeated for nine years, nine months and nine days (winning 122 consecutive races), two-time Olympic Champion and world record holder and as the man who continues to fight for justice and equality in sport and in  life. The film has its public world-wide premiere in September at Edwin’s alma mater Morehouse College.

Following the film Edwin spoke about his life and answered questions for over an hour and then went to watch the Games on the Big Screen at OLY House. Edwin said: “I was so pleased to watch the film with other Olympians, family and friends and to see their positive and sometimes emotional reactions. It was a very moving experience for me too.”

Edwin has been a regular at OLY House along with his son Julian. Edwin chatted with 94-year-old Olympian Rose Voisk who competed in the 1948 London Games. “She’s a real inspiration,” said Moses. “I just hope I have half her energy when I’m her age.”

Edwin also enjoyed watching the 400m hurdles on the Big Screen at OLY House. When his name was mentioned by the commentators when the race was about to start the crowd in the marquee in the garden clapped and cheered. Edwin said: “I’ve had such a good time at OLY House. It’s so relaxed and easy. Truly a home from home for me and my son.”

The OLY House Film Festival is showing it’s final film today: The Sirens of Ukraine. Olympians can still vote for their favourite film or documentary which will be given the Olympians Choice award. Olympians can vote here.

Edwin Moses chatting with Rose Voisk at OLY House Paris 2024.

Edwin Moses (wearing the red lanyard) watching the 400m hurdles final at OLY House.

title: Olympians are lovin’ OLY House
body:
Olympians their families and friends and members of the Olympic Family who have been to OLY House are loving it. Whether it’s chilling out with old or new friends, watching the Games on the Big Screen or watching a different sport on the other 8 screens, enjoying the food and drink or taking part in the many activities, the reaction to the WOA’s OLY House in Paris has been universally positive.

There is lots happening at OLY House. Take Thursday August 1st for example. After signing the Olympians signing wall and taking a selfie with the Paris 2024 Olympic Torch, Olympians could then have settled down to watch the Games and chat with other Olympians while they rooted on their country’s athletes competing at the Games.

They could also have gone to the two workshops being run on sport and business and OI (Olympian Intelligence), have been entertained by Mister Fred Delpla OLY who sang on the stage, watched two different films in the theatre (Personal Gold by Adam Laurent OLY and Riding Uphill), saw and heard about the genetic sequencers being used to combat doping, saw the data from the weather stations being deployed at various Olympic venues to monitor heat, humidity, wind etc or seen the programmes being run by the Japanese Olympians Association.

And for those with the stamina there was Nigeria night with a dj playing Nigerian and African music, presentations, games and a bit of dancing. For those not in Paris there was lots to do on e-OLY House, the WOA’s 24/7 home at home for Olympians during the Games to keep them connected and a part of the Paris Olympics no matter where they are.

OLY House is open from 11 am to 11 pm every day. To find out what’s on every day at OLY House, e-OLY House and at the OLY House Film Festival click here.

And don’t forget to Leave your Mark and forever be a part of the Olympic Games Paris 2024 here.

title: Jesse Owens and Luz Long among 5 awarded Olympians for Life by WOA Patron Prince Albert
body:
The granddaughters of USA’s Jesse Owens OLY and Germany’s Luz Long OLY on behalf of their grandfathers joined Kenya’s Faith Ogallo OLY, New Zealand’s Barbara Kendall OLY and Philippines’ Akiko Thomson-Guevara OLY during the Olympic Games in Paris receiving the award of Olympians for Life by WOA Patron HSH Prince Albert II of Monaco OLY and WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY.

The ceremony took place at the OLY House Paris 2024 @ Caisse d’Epargne Opening Cocktail in the presence of IOC Vice-President Nicole Hoevertsz OLY and a huge crowd of other Olympians and members of the Olympic family. The World Olympians Association’s Olympians for Life was first awarded in Rio in 2016. It celebrates those Olympians who have made significant contributions to sport and society, who have excelled both on and off the field of play.

Jesse Owens OLY and Luz Long OLY were awarded posthumously for their joint celebration at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin after the long jump competition where Owens told gold and Long silver. They walked arm in arm around the stadium as Hitler watched from the stands in a clear demonstration of the core values of the Olympic Movement and an effective rebuff to Hitler and his ideology of hate. Akiko Thomson-Guevara OLY was awarded for bringing sport to disadvantaged children, Barbara Kendall OLY for her advocacy of athletes’ rights over many years and Faith Ogallo OLY for her environmental work.

The awards for Jesse Owens OLY and Luz Long OLY were made to their granddaughters Marlene Dortch and Julia-Vanessa Long who both spoke movingly about the living legacy of their grandfathers in the ongoing fight against racism and for tolerance and acceptance of all.

Together Forever: Jesse Owens OLY and Luz Long OLY

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “Of course, every Olympian is guided by the Olympic values, but these five have gone above and beyond. What an inspiring group they are, as always. We are proud of these special Olympians whose actions inspire us all. We are used to saying Once an Olympian, always an Olympian. Well today shows that being always an Olympian even extends to beyond your life.”

The stories of these five remarkable Olympians is told below.

Watch the induction ceremony below.

See their stories here.

Akiko Thomson-Guevara OLY (Philippines) awarded for bringing sport to disadvantaged children

Faith Ogallo OLY (Kenya) awarded for her environmental work

title: 94 year old Olympian stars at OLY House Paris 2024
body:
94 year old Olympian Rose Voisk OLY was the star of the show at OLY House Paris 2024. After flying in from New York she came almost immediately to OLY House to soak up the atmosphere and enjoy the company of her fellow Olympians.

Gymnast Rose competed in the 1948 London Olympics for Yugoslavia. After her gymnastics career was over she turned to running and competed in her final marathon in 2003 at the age of 73.

Rose last came to OLY House when it was in Rio in 2016. She flew by herself to Brazil, booked an Airbnb and convinced her host to be her guide and chauffeur. They went everywhere together. When she discovered OLY House she came every day and was an inspiration to the younger Olympians.

Rose’s first stop at OLY House Paris 2024 was to sign the Olympians Signing Wall and then have a photo taken with the Paris Olympic Torch. It was then into the Grand Salon where she had a glass of champagne and was immediately surrounded by her fellow Olympians who wanted to chat with her and hear about her life adventures.

Rose said: “I love it here at OLY House. Meeting other Olympians. It’s the highlight of my time at the Olympic Games. Obviously, I love going to see the Games and watching the great athletes, who are so much stronger, fitter and technically better than in my day. But it’s the people, the other Olympians, who make the Games what they are.”

title: OLY House packed for the Olympic Games Opening Ceremony
body:
More than 225 Olympians, their families and friends came to OLY House to watch the Olympic Games Opening Ceremony on the big screen and in the Grand Salon. And online over 200 Olympians were in e-OLY House during the Opening Ceremony.

The celebrations at OLY House began hours before the Opening Ceremony started as Olympians enjoyed each other’s company and the free food and drink.

After signing the Olympians signing wall and taking a selfie with the Olympic Torch, the Olympians settled down outside in the Garden and inside in the Grand Salon. Luckily, the big marquee in the garden saved those outside from the rain.

Once the Opening Ceremony began the fun really got going. As the boat of their country went by Olympians would grab the Olympic torch and run around the Grand Salon, waving the torch about as the rest of the Olympians clapped and cheered. The Games truly bring people together from all over the world.

OLY House Paris 2024 @ Caisse d’Epargne, the Olympians’ home from home at the Games, is open every day from 11 am to 11 pm. And e-OLY House, the Olympian’s home at home during the Games is open online 24/7. Find out about everything that’s going on here.

If you haven’t registered yet for OLY House or e-OLY House you can do so here.

And don’t forget to be a part of the Paris Games forever when you Leave your Mark. Before the Opening Ceremony had even finished over 200 Olympians have left their mark here.

title: OLY House Paris 2024 opens today and Leave your Mark is back
body:
OLY House, the Olympians home from home at the Olympic Games, opens today. If you are in Paris and want to watch the Opening Ceremony on the big screen along with your fellow Olympians, then come on by. OLY House is open every day during the Games from 11 am to 11 pm. So don’t miss out on all the great activities and the chance to catch up with old friends and have a free drink or two and some food.  

Whether you are in Paris or not, you can be a part of the Olympic Games in Paris forever. How? Simply by joining Olympians from all over the world to Leave your Mark. Add your name, your autograph and the hometown you want to show on the Leave your Mark map. We had over 2,000 Olympians who left their mark in the Tokyo 2020 and Beijing 2022 editions. It’s quick and easy to Leave your Mark on our online platform HERE. 

After the Games, you will receive an exclusive downloadable souvenir poster created from the marks collected by all Olympians as a permanent memory of your contribution to the Olympic Games Paris 2024.

You don’t need to come to Paris to join in the fun. Come to e-OLY House, your home at home for the Games and chat with other Olympians and take part in lots of interesting activities. Register for e-OLY House and OLY House HERE. 

Find out about everything that is happening at OLY House and e-OLY House HERE.

And don’t forget about the two panel discussions this weekend. On Saturday it’s Enhancing Life Outside Sport for Olympians and Elite Athletes and on Sunday it’s Science, Technology and AI in Sport. There’s complimentary lunch after. If you’d like to see interesting presentations and take part in some lively discussion  RSVP HERE.

title: Have your say at the OLY House Film Festival
body:
The first ever OLY House Film Festival starts Sunday and you as an Olympian get to vote for the Olympians Choice award. The films are either made by Olympians or are about the Olympic Movement and the spirit that guides us all.

The films will be shown live most evenings from July 28 to August 10 at the OLY House Theater in Paris at 1900 CET and live and then on demand at e-OLY House, our online home at home for Olympians which is open 24/7 throughout the Games.

Twenty-five films will be featured including films about boxing, weightlifting, cricket, surfing, artistic swimming and more. Three examples.

In Strong Grandma ninety-five-year-old Catherine Kuehn, a world record-winning powerlifter, reflects on the love and loss that brought her to this moment as she prepares for her last competition.

Reconnect is a documentary about professional kitesurfer and three-time world champion Jalou Langeree, who candidly discusses her career-long battle with depression while highlighting mental health issues and gender inequality in elite sport.

Winds of Change tells the story of Olympian and IOC Young Leader Sophia Papamichalopoulos from Cyprus, who aimed to unite young Greek and Turkish Cypriots by achieving the impossible: sailing around the politically divided island to challenge, empower, and inspire unity through sport.

For the full schedule click here. 

There will be four awards: Best feature length film, best short, the jury’s prize and the Olympians Choice. The jury is film producer and president of the European Film Academy Mike Downey, WOA president and 5-time Olympian Joël Bouzou OLY and cinematographer Konstantin Esadze. 

You can cast your vote for the Olympians Choice award at e-OLY House. We’ll send you information about that tomorrow.

title: A week to go to OLY House and e-OLY House
body:
Come join us at OLY House and e-OLY House from next Friday, July 26th. We hope to see all Olympians who are in Paris at OLY House Paris 2024 @ Caisse d’Epargne. We’re open from 1100-2300 every day during the Games. And you can bring a guest or two with you. You can watch the Games on the Big Screen in the beautiful garden, enjoy the company of fellow Olympians, have some food and drink and take part in the many events there.

You can also come to e-OLY House from anywhere at any time. It’s open 24/7 with lots of interesting and fun events and activities.

Find out more about OLY House and e-OLY House and see the daily schedule of events here.

OLY House Registration

One registration will gain you entry to both OLY House and e-OLY House. If you are coming to Paris, you can also register when you arrive but doing it in advance will speed up your entry. Please register here.

OLY House Opening Cocktail

The OLY House Opening Cocktail in the presence of our Patron HSH Prince Albert II of Monaco OLY will take place on Monday July 29th at 1700. Entry for the event is by RSVP only. You may get your invitation here. We are limited to 400 guests for health and safety reasons so we will be allocating places by ballot.

OLY House Film Festival

WOA will host its first ever OLY House Film Festival. The Festival will showcase films made by Olympians or about the Olympic Movement. You’ll be able to see the films in the Theatre at OLY House and also online at e-OLY House. There will be short and feature length films and documentaries, Q&As and an awards ceremony. And you’ll be able to vote for the Olympians Choice Award. More details here.

NOA Update with WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY is inviting all National Olympians Associations to join him in the OLY House Theatre to hear about the WOA, our activities and our plans for the next four-year cycle. There are two sessions, one on August 1st and one on August 2nd. Both start at 1400.

For any questions, please contact us at olyhouse@thewoa.org.

See you in Paris or online. Enjoy the Games.

The WOA Team

title: Olympians: Register now to visit OLY House Paris 2024 and e-OLY House
body:
OLY House Paris 2024 @ Caisse d’Epargne is your home from home at the Olympic Games. And e-OLY House is your online home at home (or anywhere else) for the Games. One registration will gain you entry to both.  If you are coming to Paris you can also register when you arrive but doing it in advance will speed up your entry. Please register here.

You can bring a guest or two with you, space permitting. As OLY House is in a beautiful historic listed building not normally open to the public we had to get a special license which limits us to 400 people in the building at any one time. So, at peak times there may need to be a queuing system. And you must accompany your guests.

There’s lots going on at OLY House. You can watch the Games on the big screen, enjoy food and drink and the company of other Olympians and take part in the many events that will be happening over the 17 days. Find out more here.

If you can’t make it to Paris or are only here for a few days, you can join in the fun from wherever you are at e-OLY House, our online platform exclusively for Olympians provided by SpatialChat and open 24/7 throughout the Games.

e-OLY House will have online conference rooms and lounges, content from OLY House, exclusive content and access to the OLY House Film Festival. And you can chat with your fellow Olympians as your avatar moves around e-OLY House.

All the information about OLY House and e-OLY House is here.

For any questions about registration or anything else, please contact us at olyhouse@thewoa.org.

title: WOA Welcomes New Member Associations from Grenada, Maldives, and Palestine
body:
The WOA General Assembly has approved three new National Olympians Associations (NOAs) as members, expanding its global network. The new member associations are from Grenada, Maldives, and Palestine, bringing the total number of NOAs to 111.

Maldives Olympians Association President, Shajan Aminath OLY, expressed her enthusiasm: “Joining the WOA family is a significant milestone for us. We are excited to provide our Olympians with the support and resources they need to continue making a positive impact in our community.”

Each new NOA will receive full support from the WOA, including guidance from Development Officers who played a key role in helping these associations meet the membership criteria. These NOAs are eligible to apply for the annual WOA Development Grant and the Service to Society/Service to Olympians grants and will benefit from a range of other resources offered by WOA.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY welcomed the new members, stating: “We are thrilled to welcome Grenada, Maldives, and Palestine to the WOA family. Their inclusion strengthens our community and allows us to spread the Olympic Values to even more regions around the world. Our thanks go out to the Executive Committee, the WOA team, the NOAs who voted, and our new members for their dedication and hard work.”

The new NOAs will have the opportunity to participate in the upcoming WOA Extraordinary General Assembly in Lausanne, Switzerland in October, joining other member associations.

Olympians interested in joining their NOA can refer to the NOA Directory. For those in countries without an NOA who are interested in starting one, the NOA Start-Up Guide and the WOA team at info@thewoa.org are available for assistance.

title: Full University scholarships on offer again from WOA
body:
The WOA University of London scholarship programme is now open for applications. For the fifth year in a row, we are offering four full scholarships for Olympians to pursue a Postgraduate Certificate (PGCert) in International Sports Management from the prestigious University of London. The first thirty unsuccessful full scholarship applicants will be offered 25% scholarships.

The fully online, flexible programme is designed for Olympians at any career stage, with intakes in September 2024 and February 2025. This initiative, in partnership with the World Academy of Sport, has empowered over 60 Olympians since its inception in 2020, providing them with valuable skills and career opportunities in sports management.

The PGCert can be applied to a Master’s degree for those wishing to continue their studies to the next level. More information can be found here.

Apply for the WOA scholarship for Olympians only HERE before 4 August 2024, 17:00 CET.

title: OLY House Paris to be at an historic location
body:
OLY House, the WOA hospitality house for Olympians, formerly known as the Olympians Reunion Centre, will be at the iconic Paris headquarters of the French bank group Caisse d'Epargne. Caisse d’Epargne, a Premium Partner of both the Olympic Games Paris 2024 and the Paralympic Games Paris 2024 and the Sponsor of the Olympic Torch Relay, is providing its building for the WOA to host Olympians from around the world during the Olympic Games in Paris.

Located in the 7th arrondissement of Paris at 5 Rue Masseran, the Caisse d'Epargne headquarters is  classified as an historic monument by the French Ministry of Culture and is not normally open to the public. It follows in the tradition of previous OLY Houses located at other iconic locations such as the Customs House in Sydney in 2000, the Prince Jun Palace in Beijing in 2008, and the Wellington Barracks in London in 2012.

As in the past, OLY House with Caisse d'Epargne will be open every day during the Games. It has a great garden and there will be a big screen to watch the Games. OLY House will once again be supported by the IOC, which will promote its benefits and services for Olympians there, and will host events run by International Federations, National Olympic Committees and other NGOs.

Information for Olympians on how to pre-register and the events schedule at OLY House and e-OLY House will be sent out soon. Olympians can bring along their families and friends and can also register on the day. For health and safety reasons if OLY House nears capacity there may need to be a queuing system. Those who can’t make it to Paris will be able to join in on e-OLY House which will be open 24/7.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said, "Once again, we have found the ideal venue to welcome Olympians during the Olympic Games Paris 2024. Thanks to our close collaboration with the International Olympic Committee and its generous support, we are able to provide Olympians and other members of the Olympic Family with a top-quality environment during the Olympic Games in Paris. And thanks to the French Olympians Association President and WOA Executive Committee Member Valèrie Barlois, who helped to connect us with Caisse d’Epargne, we will benefit from a venue steeped in history and the common values of the Olympic Movement."

IOC Sports Director Kit McConnell said: “Recognizing the importance of the Olympian community for the Olympic Movement, the IOC is delighted that its support for Olympians is enabling WOA to provide another quality OLY House at such an iconic location. This is one of the many ways that the IOC supports Olympians and elite athletes both at the Games and throughout their life beyond sport.” 

Alain Di Crescenzo, President of the National Federation of Caisse d’Epargne, stated, "We are delighted to offer a meeting place for Olympians from around the world during the Paris Olympics because we share a common belief that sport is a powerful tool for cohesion and social inclusion. For Caisse d’Epargne, a Premium Partner of the Olympic Games Paris 2024 and Paralympic Games Paris 2024, hosting OLY House reflects our commitment to being helpful to athletes, territories, and society."

title: 30 Olympian-led projects awarded WOA Grants
body:
Thirty projects from 25 countries have been awarded the 2024 WOA Service to Olympians and Service to Society Grants and will be delivered in the coming months.

Using rowing to enhance students’ well-being in underserved schools in United States, providing training and competition for weightlifting athletes led by the Philippines’s first Olympic gold medallist and creating safe, accessible recreation spaces for community cohesion in Fiji are examples of Olympian grant awardees leveraging sport and the Olympic values to drive social change.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said:

“As pledged to the Global Alliance for the Promotion of Physical Activity, I am glad there were many NOAs and Olympians that have taken up the mantle to deliver sport and physical activity projects benefiting their communities. It is important for us to maintain an active lifestyle throughout our lives and also inspire all to keep fit for physical and mental health.”

Zambia Olympians Association President Jonathan Chipalo OLY added:

“With the WOA grant, 150 children will benefit from our eight-week project to eradicate childhood obesity through fitness exercises. Our Olympians will also participate and organise a fun competition for the kids, which we hope will increase the love and enjoyment of physical activity from a young age. Olympians will not only lead the talk but also walk the walk.”

title: Taiwan Olympians boost spirits at university devastated by earthquake
body:
Chinese Taipei Olympians Association members led by chairman Huang Zhixiong OLY have visited the disaster-struck National Dong Hwa University to raise awareness and support for reconstruction efforts following the severe damage caused by the recent earthquake. They brought with them supplies and funds donated by Tokyo 2020 Olympic gold medalists and other renowned Olympians.

President Xu Huiming of National Dong Hwa University, upon receiving the donations, expressed the university’s gratitude saying that the contribution from the Taiwan Olympians significantly boosted the spirits of both faculty and students.  He also announced plans for longer-term cooperation with the Chinese Taipei Olympians Association (CTOA) to promote the Olympic spirit.

Hualien was tragically struck by a series of powerful earthquakes from April to May, the largest measuring 7.2 on the Richter scale. These devastating quakes resulted in nine deaths, caused the collapse of several buildings, and inflicted severe damage to the teaching facilities at National Dong Hwa University.

CTOA Chairman Huang, who took the lead in urging Olympians to show their support for the disaster-stricken area, said: “Resilience and a spirt of mutual assistance are key core values of athletes. CTOA stands with you. Our hearts and condolences go out to those that have been affected.”

title: WOA President joins Paris Olympics Torch Relay
body:
Photo credit: Paris 2024 / Nathan Lainé / SIPA PRESS

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY has had the honour of being a torch bearer on the 10th stage of the Paris Olympics Torch relay. He ran on the stage through the Gers French Department, which is nicknamed “Little Tuscany” thanks to its quality of life, the beauty of its countryside and its many medieval villages.

Within Gers is Auch, Joël's childhood home, which has been awarded the “Active Sporting City”, “Sport and Health”, “Land of the 2024 Games” and “Olympic Games preparation centre” labels for its citizens active participation in sport.

Joël said on completing his run: “It was so exciting to run with the Olympic torch where I was brought up as a child. This is truly a dream come true. And thankfully my years of modern pentathlon training meant I was still in good enough shape to make it through with plenty of energy to spare.”

This is the first time that a current WOA President has been honoured in this way. And for those of you Olympians, your families and friends and Olympic Family members coming to OLY House in Paris during the Olympic Games this year there will be an Olympic Torch for you to take a selfie with.

title: Nominate an Olympian to join the Olympians for Life honour roll
body:
Do you know of a summer Olympian who has made a real impact both on and off the field of play? Someone who has achieved in sport and life, whether through community service, advocacy, or an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place.

At each edition of the Games we award five Olympians, one from each continent, the prestigious title of Olympians for Life. We are seeking nominations of active or retired summer Olympians who you think should be honoured during Paris 2024. Here are two awardees from Rio.

Tegla Loroupe (KEN) 

Bringing together divided communities, promoting peace and progress 

“I grew up in a conflict zone. I lost relatives. Becoming an Olympian meant overcoming difficulties, hard work and having respect. Without peace, the children don’t have time for education; there is no hope for progress. Disarming one bad person saves many lives. As an Olympian I have an obligation to speak out and to give back."

James D. Wolfensohn (AUS) 1933-2020

A life devoted to justice and equitable development

"Walking into the Olympic Stadium I realised literally for the first time that I was part of a global community. I felt empowered and wanted to empower people everywhere. That led me to try to tackle major global challenges such as peace, education, social justice, corruption, health and the environment, and guided my work in life and as President of the World Bank.”

You can see the full list of Olympians for Life inductees from previous Games here. 

To submit a nomination, send an email to info@thewoa.org by 17 May 2024. Please include the Olympian’s name, country and a summary of their contribution to society beyond the field of play. Help us inspire the world by recognizing the Olympians who embody the true spirit of Olympism.

title: Apply today for fully funded masters in Sport Ethics and Integrity
body:
Olympians can apply now for a full scholarship for the Erasmus Mundus Master in Sport Ethics and Integrity (MAiSI) funded by the IOC Olympic Solidarity programme.

This world-class two-year masters degree is taught by six leading universities in multiple European locations.

The scholarship covers all tuition fees and includes a generous travel grant and monthly stipend of €1000. For more information, including entry requirements, click here.

Alumni of the programme work in organisations such as the IOC, IPC, World Athletics, National Anti-Doping Organisations, National Olympic Committees, and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime. Many go on to undertake full scholarship PhD programmes.

Shajan Aminath OLY, President of the Maldives NOA and Deputy Minister of Sport, Fitness and Recreation in Maldives, says “MAiSI was an eye-opening journey for me. I learned about pressing issues in sports through countless stories and case studies. The classes were not only fascinating but also provided ample networking opportunities.

Being part of the Erasmus Mundus program, MAiSI took me on a transformative adventure navigating different university systems and embarking on a new journey in a different country each semester. 

What sets MAiSI apart, though, are the incredible friendships forged with people from all corners of the globe. Two years spent with colleagues from diverse backgrounds allowed me to immerse myself in their cultures, savor unique cuisines, and build unbreakable bonds month after month. MAiSI truly is an aMAiSIng program!”

Education Team member at the International Testing Agency, Nikki Hamblin OLY added, “I am so grateful for the opportunity I was given through the Olympic Solidarity scholarship to complete MAiSI. The programme gave me the tools to contribute to the integrity of sport and to the protection of athletes. The exposure to experts in academia and the professional world guided and inspired me and I am proud to be a member of a global alumni group who are making a positive difference.”

You can check out the work of the MAiSI alumni on their Instagram account The Sport Ethics Examiner.

For any questions about the programme, please contact:

Prof Dr. Mike McNamee, MAiSI Programme Director: mike.mcnamee@kuleuven.be

Don’t delay. Scholarship applications close on April 1, 2024. Apply directly to MAiSI here.

title: Japan and Indonesia NOAs work together to deliver community projects
body:
After successfully running her WOA Service to Society grant funded clothed swimming project in Japan, Kyoko Iwasaki OLY has now helped the Indonesian Olympians run a similar project in Jakarta.

Olympians from Japan and Indonesia conducted the clothed swimming workshop last weekend for over 50 students and teachers. Students learnt how to self-rescue in emergency situations using everyday household items like water bottles.

Kyoko commented, "I was very happy to work with my fellow Olympians from Indonesia. They were instrumental in sorting the venues, making the arrangements with the schools and delivering the workshop with us. I look forward to continuing our friendship with Indonesia and hope to expand the project to another Asian country in the future."

After the swimming, the Japan NOA (OAJ) Olympians' Action Project which addresses the plastic waste problem was also run at Sakura Beach on Untung Jawa island. Over 30 Indonesian Olympians participated in cleaning up the beach and ensuring proper trash disposal including Rosiana Tendean OLY who said, "I believe small actions can go a long way. Our competitive career may be over but our duty to contribute and inspire never ends."

OAJ President Mikako Kotani OLY added "We are proud to have started the Olympians' Action Project in 2023 in Japan thanks to WOA project grant funding. We passed on the same tongs for litter-picking to the Philippines NOA who organised a beach clean-up as part of their event in Palawan last October. We are glad that we are also able to continue this initiative with the Olympians in Indonesia."

Indonesia NOA President Yayuk Basuki OLY said, "It is our moral obligation to take part in making a better society such as raising and dealing with the global environmental issue and teaching the next generation.

"We would like to thank the OAJ and their partners Japan Sports SDGs Association, the Japanese government and also our Sports Ministry and BASARNAS for their support which allowed us to execute the project successfully in Indonesia. We look forward to future collaborations with Japan and also other NOAs."

title: Apply now for the 2024-25 SimiSleighs Athlete Grant
body:
WOA’s Olympian for Life awardee Simidele Adeagbo OLY has launched the second year of the Athlete Grant programme through her SimiSleighs Foundation.

The Athlete Grant is a one-year programme for female athletes who have established themselves in their chosen sports as Olympic or Paralympic athletes and hopefuls. It empowers female athletes from around the world by providing financial assistance of up to $10,000 USD for training and competition expenses, meaningful personal and professional development experiences and access to a global network.

The upcoming programme year starts this April and will run through March 2025.

Applications are open to female athletes training to represent their country at the Paris 2024 and Milano-Cortina 2026 Olympic or Paralympic Games. Applicants must be fluent in English and at least 18 years old.

See the eligibility requirements and programme guidelines here.   

Submit your application here. Applications must be received by Sunday, February 11, 2024 at 11:59 pm Eastern Standard Time.

title: Holiday wishes from WOA
body:
Dear fellow Olympians,

As we come to the end of another eventful year, I would like to thank you all for your dedication and hard work promoting the Olympic values in your communities. We were delighted to see your many projects and events that served either the needs of your communities or your fellow Olympians. We always try to promote them on our website and social media. If you participated in a project that could inspire or be copied by your fellow Olympians, please share the details here and we’ll do a story or social about it: Best Practices Form.

A big highlight of 2023 was the third World Olympians Forum which was held in Istanbul. It was attended by 150 Olympians from over 100 countries. Delegates exchanged best practices, heard from world experts and participated in workshops on how Olympians can more effectively spread the values of the Olympic Movement, the benefits of sport and physical activity and give back to their communities. The Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was fulsome in his praise, saying: ““I was so impressed with the level of knowledge and debate and the ideas that emerged from the World Olympians Forum”. We were very grateful for his and his city’s hospitality and dedication to sport as a tool for peace, health and social integration.

The WOA continued to grow this year. The WOA General Assembly voted in 12 new National Olympians Associations in May. The new member associations are based in: Algeria, Benin, Bulgaria, Cameroon, Czech Republic, Equatorial Guinea, Eswatini, Lesotho, Mauritius, Saudi Arabia, Sierra Leone and Venezuela. We will continue to support these budding organisations and encourage the formation of new NOAs in the new year.

Olympian opportunities continued to be offered to all Olympians, including full and partial scholarships for the University of London’s Postgraduate Certificate in International Sports Management in partnership with the World Academy of Sport. If you know of any upcoming opportunities specific to Olympians, please do not hesitate to contact us with the relevant information.

Service to Society and Service to Olympians grants for Olympian-led projects were awarded across all five continents, including an impressive list of activities such as an all women, all ages skate competition in South Africa. In June I announced at the Global Alliance for Physical Activity Summit in Hamburg that all Service to Society grants next year would be reserved for projects that get people physically active. Applications for those grants will open in early January.

There were many OLY Celebrations in 2023, including the largest-ever gathering of Olympians in Chilean history which took place right before the Santiago 2023 Pan American and Parapan American games in October. Uplifting and recognising Olympians is a priority every year and we will continue to support and promote OLY celebrations in 2024.

We celebrated passing the 20,000 mark for OLY registrations this year. If you know of any Olympian who hasn’t signed up yet, make sure to tell them and share this link so they can join our ever-growing OLY community.

Finally, I would like to thank the IOC for their continued support, the WOA Executive Committee, WOA CEO and our staff and you all for your dedication to our Olympian community and your promotion of the Olympic values. Without you, fellow Olympians, there would be no Olympics. Without your work and dedication, the Olympic Movement would be the poorer. You are the living embodiment of the spirit that guided Pierre de Coubertin when he revived the Olympics. Don’t ever forget that.

We hope you have a relaxing and festive holiday season in the company of your families and friends. Enjoy the celebrations. And let’s all come back in the new year refreshed and ready to promote together a healthy and physically active 2024.

I hope to be able to see many of you at OLY House in Paris, whether in person or online. We will send you more details about the OLY House activities early next year. All the best for 2024. And bonne chance to those of you who will be competing at the Paris Games.

Best Olympian regards to you all.

Joël Bouzou OLY
President

title: Kosovo Olympians to get their own association
body:
The Kosovo Olympic Committee has pledged to help Olympians in its country set up a Kosovo Olympians Association. WOA Executive Committee member Igor Boraska OLY has met with Kosovo Olympic Committee President Mr. Ismet Krasniqi to discuss the formation of the association.

President Krasniqi expressed the willingness and readiness of the KOC to establish the Kosovo National Olympians Association as soon as possible in close cooperation with the World Olympians Association.

Boraska congratulated President Krasniqi on Kosovo’s successes already achieved as one of the newest National Olympic Committees. Kosovo has won three Olympic gold medals in its first two summer Olympic Games, one at Rio 2016 and two at Tokyo 2020.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “We thank Mr. Krasniqi for his warm welcome of our executive committee member Igor Boraska OLY. We are looking forward to working with the KOC to help Kosovo Olympians form their National Olympians Association so that they can serve the needs of Kosovo Olympians and empower them to spread the values of the Olympic movement and use the power of sport to give back to their communities.”

title: 98-year-old Venezuelan Olympian awarded his OLY
body:
Venezuela’s first Olympian, Julio César León OLY (Cycling, 1948), has been awarded his OLY certificate and pin at his home in Caracas.

The 98-year-old Olympian was personally visited by Venezuelan Association of Olympic Athletes President, four-time Olympian in fencing Alejandra Benítez OLY, Venezuelan Olympic Committee President and Olympian in softball, Maria Soto OLY, as well as the general secretary, judoka Katiuska Santaella OLY, together with WOA Americas Development Officer, Inés Remersaro OLY.

The next day saw the founding General Assembly of the Venezuela Olympians Association in the auditorium of the Venezuelan Olympic Committee. 61 Olympians were there representing four generations and ten Olympic Games ranging from Munich 1972 to Tokyo 2020.

Among them were the first female Venezuelan Olympic medalist, Adriana Carmona OLY, bronze in Barcelona 1992 and Athens 2004 (Taekwondo-Barcelona 1992, Sydney 2000, Athens 2004 and Beijing 2008), Stefany Hernández OLY bronze in Rio 2016 (BMX Cycling- London 2012, Rio 2016), and Rostín González (Basketball- Barcelona 1992).

Venezuelan Olympians Association President Alejandra Benítez OLY said: "We thank the WOA for the support through our Service to Olympians grant. We are very happy to have held our first recognition ceremonies for our Olympians. It was a very emotional and special event as we were able to give our first Olympian his certificate and OLY pin, as well as the 61 Olympians who were present in the VOC auditorium." 

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY said: “We are delighted to see our Service to Olympians grant put to such excellent use. Recognising the first Olympian from Venezuela is a proud moment and we thank the Venezuelan Olympians Association for all their hard work.  OLY recognises the achievements of Olympians and their commitment to use the Olympic values and the power of sport to make the world a better place. We wish the 61 Olympians honoured at the General Assembly all the best for the future.”

title: Chilean Olympians make history in Santiago
body:
The largest ever gathering of Olympians in Chilean history took place just before the Santiago 2023 Pan American and Parapan American Games, which will kick off later this month. Panam Sports President Neven Ilic, NOC Chile President Miguel Angel Mujica and Santiago 2023 Executive Director Harold Mayne-Nicholls were among the dignitaries who were present as seventy-five Chilean Olympians were awarded their prestigious OLY certificates and pins.

NOA Chile President Miguel Droguett OLY said: “We are honoured to have the presence today of Panam Sports President Neven Ilic and NOC Chile President Miguel Angel Mujica. On behalf of the Chilean Olympians Association, I would like to thank them both for their support, as well as the WOA and our sponsors whose financial contributions made this event possible. Congratulations to all my fellow Olympians honoured today.’’

WOA President Joel Bouzou OLY said: “We are so happy to see our Service to Olympians grant awarded to the Chilean Olympians Association put to such good use. OLY recognises the achievements of Olympians and their commitment to use the Olympic values and the power of sport to make the world a better place. We salute the 75 Chilean Olympians honoured in Santiago and wish them all the best for the future.” 

Among the celebrated Olympians were:

  • Paris Inostroza OLY (Fencing – Atlanta 1996, Athens 2004, Beijing 2008, London 2012)
  • Isidora Jiménez OLY (Athletics – Rio 2016)
  • Erika Olivera OLY (Athletics – Atlanta 1996, Sidney 2000, Athens 2004, London 2012, Rio 2016)
  • Gert Weil OLY (Athletics – Los Angeles 1984, Seoul 1988, Barcelona 1992, Atlanta 1996)
  • Annegret Weller OLY and Betty Kretschmer OLY (Athletics – London 1948)

Panam Sports President, Neven Ilic, closed the event telling the 75 Olympians present: “Congratulations to all of you for your great efforts that led you to represent our Chile at the Olympic Games. It would be an honour to have you all at the Opening Ceremony of Santiago 2023. I formally invite you to attend and look forward to welcoming you soon.”

title: Istanbul mayor praises World Olympians Forum 2023
body:
Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu has praised the 150 Olympians from all over the world who came to Istanbul for two days of discussion, debate and learnings.

Over 100 countries were represented at the third World Olympians Forum whose aim was to spread best practices, hear from world experts and workshop how Olympians can more effectively spread the values of the Olympic Movement, the benefits of sport and physical activity and give back to their communities.

“I was so impressed with the level of knowledge and debate and the ideas that emerged from the World Olympians Forum,” said Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu who had given a keynote speech as part of the official opening ceremony along with welcome video messages from WOA Patron HSH Prince Albert II of Monaco OLY and WOA Honorary President, IOC President Thomas Bach OLY.

Mayor Imamoglu continued: “Our city is committed to the promotion of physical activity and sport to ensure our citizens can be as healthy and as happy as possible and so we can reverse the growing scourge of obesity and avoidable illness in our communities. At the World Olympians Forum we heard many ideas that can help us in our quest.”

The aim of the World Olympians Forum was to inspire and upskill Olympians and National Olympians Association representatives. The delegates heard from world experts including IOC Medical Commission member Professor Yannis Pitsiladis who spoke about the Global Alliance for the Promotion of Physical Activity and why the Global Alliance was so badly needed.  

Topics ranging from leveraging your Olympian image and developing Olympian leaders to creating a social business and fostering philanthropy for a better world were presented by the World Academy of Sport, the Yunus Sports Hub, the King Baudouin Foundation, Skillsbuild, Egoli founder Caroline Rowland and Dr Noemi Zaharia OLY.

An IOC Athletes Commission panel led by Chair Emma Terho OLY and moderated by IOC Athletes’ Department Director Kaveh Mehrabi OLY discussed the many IOC Athlete365 programmes and opportunities that can benefit Olympians and exchanged ideas on how National Olympians Associations and National Olympic Committee Athletes’ Commissions can work closely together to spread the values of the Olympic Movement and run programmes in their communities.

Spor Istanbul head Renay Onur spoke about the Istanbul Journey and how big cities and Olympians can work together to promote healthy lifestyles and the joys of sport and physical activity.   

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY was very pleased with the outcome of the two days. He said: "This has been the best World Olympians Forum ever and shows how far we have come in the past eight years, the level of maturity our National Olympians Associations have achieved and the abilities of Olympians all over the world to help with social cohesion, bringing sport to disadvantaged communities, protecting the environment and teaching our young citizens the positive values of sport and the Olympic Movement.

“I would like to thank our generous hosts, the Istanbul Metropolitan Authority, and in particular Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, whose infectious enthusiasm and deep understanding of the power of sport and physical activity to change society for the better was an inspiration to us all.”

The World Olympians Forum 2023 was livestreamed on the Turkish television network Sportstv and online on the WOA’s e-WOF digital platform. The World Olympians Forum 2023 is also available worldwide on demand on the Sportstv app.

title: World Olympians Forum will also be live streamed
body:
The World Olympians Forum (WOF) will kick off this weekend, taking place physically in Istanbul and live-streamed online on the newly created e-WOF. Over 150 Olympians from WOA member organisations will meet in Istanbul for the third World Olympians Forum. NOA members that are not able to attend in person are able to join the e-WOF and participate online.

The e-WOF will showcase the official opening graced by the Mayor of Istanbul Ekrem Imamoglu along with WOA President Joel Bouzou OLY, WOA Patron HSH Prince Albert II of Monaco OLY and WOA Honorary President and IOC President Thomas Bach OLY. There will be workshop sessions led by world leading experts and NOAs will share their best practices and contribute to strengthening the Olympian networks across the globe.

WOA President Joel Bouzou OLY said: “This will be the best World Olympians Forum yet. We are excited to welcome our members from all over the world to the beautiful city of Istanbul. They will make great connections and exchange ideas that will help them contribute to their societies and fellow Olympians back home. For Olympians that are not able to join us in person, we hope they are able to join us online in the e-WOF.”

The WOA Executive Committee will hold their annual in-person meeting prior to the WOF.

NOA executive committee members that are interested to attend the e-WOF can contact us at  ewof@thewoa.org

title: Four more Olympians awarded full scholarships
body:
Four Olympians have been awarded the postgraduate scholarship offered by World Academy of Sport and World Olympians Association. They will begin the University of London’s International Sports Management programme in the academic year 2023/24.

The WOA full scholarship recipients are:

  • Bayan Jumah OLY – Syria, Swimming
  • Ravi Bhollah OLY – Mauritius, Weightlifting
  • Maike Helga Diekmann OLY – Namibia, Rowing
  • Ganzi Mugula OLY- Uganda, Swimming

Bayan Jumah OLY was the first Syrian swimmer to qualify for the Olympic Games  and the first to win an Asian gold. She also founded the Bayan Jumah Swimming Academy in Aleppo, Syria, a symbol of resilience and hope in a time of adversity. She hopes to use the scholarship to adapt to her new professional life in France and continue to give back.

Ravi Bhollah OLY is an accomplished Olympic weightlifter, participating in the Beijing 2008 Games. He is also a skilled and passionate coach. One of his proudest achievements is coaching an athlete to secure 4th place at the 2019 World Youth Weightlifting Championships, the highest rank ever achieved by a Mauritian weightlifter at this level. He plans on using the skills gained through this scholarship to make a difference at the federation level to benefit athletes.

Maike Helga Diekmann OLY was the first Namibian rower to compete at an Olympic Games. She currently serves as an Athletes Representative on the Executive Board of the Namibia National Olympic Committee and Commonwealth Games Association. She will apply the knowledge gained through the scholarship to her current work at an international federation, supporting athletes worldwide.

Ganzi Mugula OLY was the team captain and flag-bearer for Uganda in the London 2012 Games. He is the Athletes Representative on the NOC Executive Committee, and has run IOC athlete pathway programmes in Uganda. He will use the scholarship to transition into a career in sports administration and continue to support athletes in all stages of their lives.

WOA President Joël Bouzou OLY personally congratulated the four Olympians, saying:

“At WOA we are delighted to provide this scholarship to such accomplished Olympians. We are confident they will use this opportunity to give back to their communities. WOA is looking forward to offering further scholarships through our partnership with the World Academy of Sport so that more Olympians can benefit.”

Applications for partly funded scholarships beginning in February 2024 are still open. The course is time-flexible, remote and designed to allow completion at your own pace. You can submit your application HERE before Friday 13 October 2023 at 1700 Lausanne time.

title: NOA Portugal celebrates its female Olympians
body:
The Association of Olympic Athletes of Portugal recently celebrated its 20th anniversary with a tribute to the "bravas do pelotão," the 137 women Olympians who have represented Portugal from Helsinki 1952 to Tokyo 2020. The event took place at the New Cruise Terminal of the Port of Leixões and was attended by about 200 Olympians, of which more than 40 were honoured.

The president of Portugal, Professor Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa, sent a special video message for the event. Speakers at the event included Professor Sameiro Araújo of NOC Portugal, Carlos Pereira from the Portuguese Institute of Youth and Sport and Vasco Pinho, Sports Councillor from the Motosinhos City Council.

AAOP President Luis Alves Monteiro OLY said: “We want to create a strong community through the Olympic spirit that has the capacity to give back to society. The partners who were present left deeply satisfied because they realised they are investing in the right cause because we work for the athletes. In twenty years from now I hope to see the association as strong and capable as ever.”

Fernanda Ribeiro OLY said: “It feels great to be celebrated with my fellow Olympians while I’m still alive . I even received calls from male athletes currently in competitions apologising for not being able to join, since they believe I deserve the recognition.

Carla Sacramento OLY added: “Honouring unity makes strength. As they say, when you want to go fast, go alone. When you want to go far, go together.”
